translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 74

sentences.zh: 【魏紀六】起著雍敦牂，盡旃蒙赤奮若，凡八年。

translations.literal: [Wei Records Six] Beginning with Zheyong Dunzhang, ending with Zhanmeng Chifenruo, eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Wei Records, Six] spans from the year Zheyong-Dunzhang through Zhanmeng-Chifenruo—a period of eight years.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝下景初二年（

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, lower scroll, Jingchu year two (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Three (conclusion), Jingchu year 2 (

sentences.zh: 戊午，公元二三八年）

translations.literal: Wuwu, the year 238 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: wuwu cycle, AD 238)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，帝召司馬懿於長安，使將兵四萬討遼東。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, the Emperor summoned Sima Yi from Chang'an and ordered him to lead forty thousand troops to campaign against Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the emperor recalled Sima Yi from Chang'an and sent him with forty thousand men to subdue Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 議臣或以為四萬兵多，役費難供。

translations.literal: Some of the councilors held that forty thousand troops were too many and that the labor costs would be hard to supply.
translations.idiomatic: Some advisers argued that forty thousand soldiers were excessive and that the expense of supplying them would be prohibitive.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「四千里征伐，雖雲用奇，亦當任力，不當稍計役費也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "A campaign four thousand li distant—though one speaks of employing stratagem, one must still rely on force; one should not fuss over labor costs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A four-thousand-li campaign may call for stratagem, but it still demands brute strength—do not penny-pinch over supply costs."

sentences.zh: 」帝謂懿曰：「公孫淵將何計以待君？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said to Yi: "What stratagem will Gongsun Yuan use against you?
translations.idiomatic: " He then asked Yi, "What plan will Gongsun Yuan adopt to meet you?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「淵棄城豫走，上計也；

translations.literal: " He replied: "If Yuan abandons his cities and flees in advance, that is the best plan;
translations.idiomatic: " Yi answered, "If Yuan abandons his cities and flees beforehand, that would be his best course;

sentences.zh: 據遼東拒大軍，其次也；

translations.literal: holding Liaodong to resist the great army would be second best;
translations.idiomatic: holding Liaodong to bar our main force would be second best;

sentences.zh: 坐守襄平，此成禽耳。

translations.literal: sitting tight in Xiangping—he will be captured for certain."
translations.idiomatic: but to sit tight in Xiangping is simply to invite capture."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然則三者何出？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Then which of the three will he choose?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Which of the three will he actually choose?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「唯明智能審量彼我，乃豫有所割棄。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Only a sage ruler who can weigh foe against self will deliberately abandon something in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Only a sage who can weigh enemy against self will deliberately sacrifice ground in advance.

sentences.zh: 此既非淵所及，又謂今往孤遠，不能支久，必先拒遼水，後守襄平也。

translations.literal: Yuan cannot reach that level; moreover he will think that we have come far and alone and cannot endure long—so he is sure first to block the Liao River, then hold Xiangping."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan lacks that capacity; he will also judge that we have marched far and alone and cannot hold out long—so he is sure to block the Liao first, then defend Xiangping."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「還往幾日？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "How many days for the round trip?"
translations.idiomatic: "How long for the round trip?" the emperor asked.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「往百日，攻百日，還百日，以六十日為休息，如此，一年足矣。

translations.literal: " He replied: "One hundred days going, one hundred days attacking, one hundred days returning, with sixty days for rest—in this fashion one year is enough."
translations.idiomatic: "One hundred days going, one hundred attacking, one hundred returning, with sixty for rest—as much as a year altogether," Yi replied.

sentences.zh: 公孫淵聞之，復遣使稱臣，求救於吳。

translations.literal: Gongsun Yuan heard this and again sent envoys declaring himself a subject, begging aid from Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongsun Yuan heard of the campaign, he again sent envoys to declare himself a vassal and beg Wu for rescue.

sentences.zh: 吳人欲戮其使，羊道曰：「不可，是肆匹夫之怒而捐霸王之計也，不如因而厚之，遣奇兵潛往以要其成。

translations.literal: The men of Wu wished to execute his envoys. Yang Dao said: "That must not be done—it would be indulging a commoner's rage while casting away a hegemon's plan. Better to treat them generously on the pretext and secretly send a daring force to reap the harvest.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu court wanted to kill the envoys, but Yang Dao said, "You must not—that would be indulging a commoner's fury while throwing away a hegemon's design. Treat them generously instead and secretly dispatch a strike force to seize whatever opportunity arises.

sentences.zh: 若魏伐不克，而我軍遠赴，是恩結遐夷，義形萬里；

translations.literal: If Wei fails in the campaign and our army goes far to their aid, we will have bound distant barbarians in gratitude and displayed righteousness across ten thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: If Wei fails to conquer and our army marches to their aid, we bind distant peoples in gratitude and show righteousness across ten thousand li;

sentences.zh: 若兵連不解，首尾離隔，則我虜其傍郡，驅略而歸，亦足以致天之罰，報雪曩事矣。

translations.literal: if the fighting drags on without end and head and tail are separated, then we can seize their neighboring commanderies, drive and plunder, and return—enough to inflict Heaven's punishment and avenge past wrongs."
translations.idiomatic: if the war drags on and their forces are stretched thin, we can raid their neighboring commanderies, plunder, and withdraw—enough to bring Heaven's judgment upon them and settle old scores."

sentences.zh: 」吳主曰：「善！

translations.literal: " The Lord of Wu said: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」乃大勒兵謂淵使曰：「請俟後問，當從簡書，必與弟同休戚。

translations.literal: " He then mustered troops on a grand scale and told Yuan's envoy: "Wait for further word; when the brief dispatch arrives, I shall surely share fortune and misfortune with your master.
translations.idiomatic: " He then staged a grand military review and told Yuan's envoy, "Await further word; when my written pledge arrives, I shall surely share your master's fortunes and misfortunes.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：司馬懿所向無前，深為弟憂之。

translations.literal: " He also said: Sima Yi advances without meeting resistance—I am deeply anxious on your master's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "Sima Yi advances wherever he turns—I am deeply worried for your master."

sentences.zh: 」帝問於護軍將軍蔣濟曰：「孫權其救遼東乎？

translations.literal: " The Emperor asked Protector of the Army Jiang Ji: "Will Sun Quan rescue Liaodong?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Protector of the Army Jiang Ji, "Will Sun Quan rescue Liaodong?

sentences.zh: 」濟曰：「彼知官備已固，利不可得，深入則非力所及，淺入則勞而無獲；

translations.literal: " Ji said: "He knows our preparations are already solid and that gain is unobtainable; a deep thrust exceeds his strength, while a shallow thrust means toil without reward;
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied, "He knows our defenses are solid and profit unobtainable; a deep thrust exceeds his strength, while a shallow raid means toil without gain;

sentences.zh: 權雖子弟在危，猶將不動，況異域之人，兼以往者之辱乎！

translations.literal: even if Quan's own kin were in peril he would still not move—how much less for men of another realm, especially given past humiliations!
translations.idiomatic: even if Quan's own kin were endangered he would not stir—how much less for a distant stranger, especially after past humiliations!

sentences.zh: 今所以外揚此聲者，譎其行人，疑之於我，我之不克，冀其折節事己耳。

translations.literal: The reason he now broadcasts this loudly is to deceive Yuan's envoys, sow doubt toward us, and hope that if we fail, Yuan will bow and serve him.
translations.idiomatic: He broadcasts this now to deceive Yuan's envoys, sow doubt about us, and hope that if we fail, Yuan will submit to him.

sentences.zh: 然沓渚之間，去淵尚遠，若大軍相守，事不速決，則權之淺規，或得輕兵掩襲，未可測也。

translations.literal: Yet between Dazhu and the sea it is still far from Yuan; if the great armies face each other and the matter is not quickly decided, Quan's shallow scheme might yet allow light troops to strike by surprise—this cannot be measured in advance."
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Dazhu to Yuan's seat is still a great distance; if our main forces stalemate and the issue is not quickly settled, Quan's shallow design might still let light troops raid by surprise—this cannot be ruled out."

sentences.zh: 帝問吏部尚書盧毓：「誰可為司徒者？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Minister of the Civil Service Lu Yu: "Who can serve as Minister over the Masses?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Minister of the Civil Service Lu Yu, "Who is fit to be Minister over the Masses?

sentences.zh: 」毓薦處士管寧。

translations.literal: " Yu recommended the reclusive scholar Guan Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Yu recommended the recluse Guan Ning.

sentences.zh: 帝不能用，更問其次，對曰：「敦篤至行，則太中大夫韓暨；

translations.literal: The Emperor could not employ him and asked for the next choice. He replied: "For honest and earnest supreme conduct, Grand Master of Palace Han Ji;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not use Ning and asked for the next name. Yu said, "For honest and earnest supreme conduct, Grand Master of Palace Han Ji;

sentences.zh: 亮直清方，則司隸校尉崔林；

translations.literal: for bright uprightness and pure integrity, Director of the Secretariat Cui Lin;
translations.idiomatic: for bright uprightness and pure integrity, Director of the Secretariat Cui Lin;

sentences.zh: 貞固純粹，則太常常林。

translations.literal: for steadfast purity, Minister of Ceremonies Chang Lin."
translations.idiomatic: for steadfast purity, Minister of Ceremonies Chang Lin."

sentences.zh: 」二月，癸卯，以韓暨為司徒。

translations.literal: " In the second month, on day Guimao, Han Ji was appointed Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day guimao, Han Ji was made Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 漢主立皇后張氏，前後之妹也。

translations.literal: The Han ruler installed Lady Zhang as empress—she was the younger sister of the former empress.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu emperor installed Lady Zhang as empress; she was the younger sister of the late empress.

sentences.zh: 立王貴人子璿為皇太子，瑤為安定王。

translations.literal: He established the son of Honored Lady Wang, Xuan, as heir apparent, and Yao as Prince of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: He named the son of Honored Lady Wang, Xuan, crown prince, and Yao Prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 大司農河南孟光問太子讀書及情性好尚於秘書郎郤正，正曰：「奉親虔恭，夙夜匪解，有古世子之風；

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture Meng Guang of Henan asked Secretary Gentleman Xi Zheng about the heir's reading and temperament. Zheng said: "In serving his parents he is reverent and respectful, untiring day and night—he has the bearing of an ancient crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Agriculture Meng Guang of Henan asked Secretary Gentleman Xi Zheng about the crown prince's studies and temperament. Zheng said, "He serves his parents with reverent devotion, untiring day and night—he has the bearing of an ancient heir apparent;

sentences.zh: 接待群僚，舉動出於仁恕。

translations.literal: in receiving the officials his conduct springs from benevolence and forbearance."
translations.idiomatic: in receiving officials his conduct springs from benevolence and forbearance."

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「如君所道，皆家戶所有耳；

translations.literal: " Guang said: "What you describe is what every household possesses;
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "What you describe is what every household possesses;

sentences.zh: 吾今所問，欲知其權略智調何如也。

translations.literal: what I ask now is to know how his strategic grasp and native wit stand."
translations.idiomatic: what I want to know is how his strategic grasp and native wit measure up."

sentences.zh: 」正曰：「世子之道，在於承志竭歡，既不得妄有施為，智調藏於胸懷，權略應時而發，此之有無，焉可豫知也！

translations.literal: " Zheng said: "The way of a crown prince lies in carrying out the will and exhausting joy in service—he must not act rashly on his own. Wit is hidden in the breast; strategy is deployed as the moment demands. Whether these exist—how can one know in advance!"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "A crown prince's duty is to carry out the will and give his utmost in service—he must not act rashly on his own. Wit lies hidden in the breast; strategy deploys as the moment demands. Whether he has these—how can one know in advance!"

sentences.zh: 」光知正慎宜，不為放談，乃曰：「吾好直言，無所迴避。

translations.literal: " Guang knew Zheng was cautious and proper and would not speak loosely, so he said: "I like straight talk and make no detours.
translations.idiomatic: Guang knew Zheng was cautious and would not speak loosely, so he said, "I favor plain speech and make no detours.

sentences.zh: 今天下未定，智意為先，智意自然，不可力強致也。

translations.literal: The realm is not yet settled; wit and intent come first—and wit and intent come naturally; they cannot be forced into being.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is unsettled; wit and intent come first—and wit and intent arise naturally; they cannot be forced.

sentences.zh: 儲君讀書，寧當效吾等竭力博識以待訪問，如博士探策講試以求爵位邪！

translations.literal: Should the heir study books only to imitate us in straining for broad learning to await interrogation, like academicians drawing lots for examination to win rank!
translations.idiomatic: Should the heir study only to imitate us in cramming broad learning for interrogation, like academicians drawing lots in examinations to win rank!

sentences.zh: 當務其急者。

translations.literal: He should attend to what is urgent."
translations.idiomatic: He should attend to what is urgent."

sentences.zh: 」正深謂光言為然。

translations.literal: " Zheng deeply held Guang's words to be correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng deeply agreed with Guang.

sentences.zh: 正，儉之孫也。

translations.literal: Zheng was the grandson of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was the grandson of Jian.

sentences.zh: 吳人鑄當千大錢。

translations.literal: The men of Wu cast large coins worth a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wu cast large coins worth a thousand cash each.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚子，南鄉恭侯韓暨卒。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on day Gengzi, the Revered Marquis of Nanxiang Han Ji died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengzi, the Revered Marquis of Nanxiang Han Ji died.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，大赦。

translations.literal: On day Gengxu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 六月，司馬懿軍至遼東，公孫淵使大將軍卑衍、楊祚將步騎數萬屯遼隧，圍塹二十餘里。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Sima Yi's army reached Liaodong. Gongsun Yuan sent Grand Generals Bei Yan and Yang Zuo to lead several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to camp at Liaosui, with entrenchments encircling more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Sima Yi's army reached Liaodong. Gongsun Yuan sent Grand Generals Bei Yan and Yang Zuo with tens of thousands of foot and horse to hold Liaosui, their trenches ringing more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲擊之，懿曰：「賊所以堅壁，欲老吾兵也，今攻之，正墮其計。

translations.literal: The generals wished to attack them. Yi said: "The rebels hold fast behind walls because they wish to wear our troops down; to attack now is exactly to fall into their plan.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to attack, but Yi said, "The enemy holds behind walls to wear us down; attacking now plays straight into their plan.

sentences.zh: 且賊大眾在此，其巢窟空虛。

translations.literal: Moreover, the rebels' main force is here and their nest is empty.
translations.idiomatic: Their main force is here, and their nest is empty.

sentences.zh: 直指襄平，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Strike straight for Xiangping and we are sure to break them."
translations.idiomatic: Strike straight for Xiangping and we are sure to break them."

sentences.zh: 」乃多張旗幟，欲出其南，衍等盡銳趣之。

translations.literal: " He then displayed many banners and flags, feigning to march out on their south; Yan and the rest rushed their best troops to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised many banners and flags as if to march out on their south; Yan and the rest rushed their best troops to meet him.

sentences.zh: 懿潛濟水，出其北，直趣襄平；

translations.literal: Yi secretly crossed the water, came out on their north, and pressed straight for Xiangping;
translations.idiomatic: Yi secretly crossed the river, emerged on their north, and pressed straight for Xiangping;

sentences.zh: 衍等恐，引兵夜走。

translations.literal: Yan and the rest were afraid and led their troops away by night.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the rest were alarmed and withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 諸軍進至首山，淵復使衍等逆戰，懿擊，大破之，遂進圍襄平。

translations.literal: The armies advanced to Shoushan. Yuan again sent Yan and the rest to give battle; Yi struck and routed them utterly, then pressed on to besiege Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: The armies advanced to Shoushan. Yuan again sent Yan and the rest to give battle; Yi struck and routed them utterly, then pressed on to besiege Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，大霖雨，遼水暴漲，運船自遼口徑至城下。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: great torrential rains; the Liao River rose in flood, and supply boats came straight from Liaokou to below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, torrential rains fell; the Liao River flooded, and supply boats sailed straight from Liaokou to the foot of the walls.

sentences.zh: 雨月餘不止，平地水數尺。

translations.literal: The rain did not cease for more than a month; on level ground the water stood several feet deep.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell for more than a month without stopping; on level ground the water stood several feet deep.

sentences.zh: 三軍恐，欲移營，懿令軍中：「敢有言徙者斬！

translations.literal: The three armies were afraid and wished to shift camp. Yi ordered the army: "Whoever speaks of moving—behead him!
translations.idiomatic: The three armies were afraid and wanted to shift camp. Yi ordered, "Whoever speaks of moving camp—behead him!

sentences.zh: 」都督令史張靜犯令，斬之，軍中乃定。

translations.literal: " Director of the Army Commandant's clerical officer Zhang Jing violated the order and was beheaded; then the army was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Army Commandant's clerical officer Zhang Jing violated the order and was beheaded; then the army settled down.

sentences.zh: 賊恃水，樵牧自若，諸將欲取之，懿皆不聽。

translations.literal: The rebels relied on the water and gathered fuel and grazed herds as they pleased; the generals wished to seize them, but Yi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels relied on the flood and gathered fuel and grazed herds as they pleased; the generals wanted to seize them, but Yi forbade it.

sentences.zh: 司馬陳珪曰：「昔攻上庸，八部俱進，晝夜不息，故能一旬之半，拔堅城，斬孟達。

translations.literal: Major Chen Gui said: "When we attacked Shangyong in the past, the eight divisions advanced together without ceasing day or night, and so in half a month we took a strong city and beheaded Meng Da.
translations.idiomatic: Major Chen Gui said, "When we attacked Shangyong, all eight divisions advanced together without ceasing day or night, and in half a month we took a strong city and beheaded Meng Da.

sentences.zh: 今者遠來而更安緩，愚竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Now we have come from afar yet grow more leisurely—I am privately puzzled."
translations.idiomatic: Now we have marched from afar yet grow more leisurely—I am puzzled."

sentences.zh: 」懿曰：「孟達眾少而食支一年，將士四倍於達而糧不淹月；

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Meng Da had few troops but provisions for a year; our officers and soldiers were four times Da's number yet grain did not last a month;
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Meng Da had few troops but provisions for a year; our officers and soldiers outnumbered him fourfold yet our grain did not last a month;

sentences.zh: 以一月圖一年，安可不速！

translations.literal: to use one month against one year—how could we not hurry!
translations.idiomatic: to spend one month against one year—how could we not hurry!

sentences.zh: 以四擊一，正令失半而克，猶當為之，是以不計死傷，與糧競也。

translations.literal: With four striking one, even if we lost half and still conquered, it was still worth doing—hence we did not count casualties but raced against grain.
translations.idiomatic: With four striking one, even losing half our force to win was still worth it—so we did not count casualties but raced against grain.

sentences.zh: 今賊眾我寡，賊饑我飽，水雨乃爾，功力不設，雖當促之，亦何所為！

translations.literal: Now the rebels are many and we few; the rebels hungry and we full; with rain and flood like this, effort cannot be deployed—even if we should urge haste, what could we accomplish!
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy outnumbers us, the enemy starves while we are fed, and with rain and flood like this effort cannot be deployed—even if we urged haste, what could we accomplish!

sentences.zh: 自發京師，不憂賊攻，但恐賊走。

translations.literal: From the time we set out from the capital I have not feared the rebels' attack but only feared the rebels' flight.
translations.idiomatic: From the time we left the capital I have not feared the enemy's attack but only feared the enemy's flight.

sentences.zh: 今賊糧垂盡而圍落未合，掠其牛馬，抄其樵采，此故驅之走也。

translations.literal: Now the rebels' grain is nearly exhausted and the encirclement is not yet closed—if we seize their cattle and horses and raid their fuel-gathering, that is precisely to drive them to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy's grain is nearly gone and the encirclement is not yet closed—seizing their cattle and raiding their woodcutters is precisely to drive them to flee.

sentences.zh: 夫兵者詭道，善因事變。

translations.literal: Warfare is the way of deception; one excels at adapting to events.
translations.idiomatic: Warfare is the way of deception; one excels at adapting to events.

sentences.zh: 賊憑眾恃雨，故雖饑困，未肯束手，當示無能以安之。

translations.literal: The rebels rely on their numbers and trust the rain; though hungry and distressed, they will not yet yield—we should show inability to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy relies on numbers and trusts the rain; though hungry and distressed, they will not yield—we should show inability to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 取小利以驚之，非計也。

translations.literal: To take small gains and startle them is not the plan."
translations.idiomatic: Taking small gains to startle them is not the plan."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷聞師遇雨，鹹欲罷兵。

translations.literal: " When the court heard the army had met rain, all wished to withdraw the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard the army had met rain, all wished to withdraw the troops.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「司馬懿臨危制變，禽淵可計日待也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Sima Yi masters danger and controls change; capturing Yuan can be awaited by counting days."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Sima Yi masters danger and adapts to change; capturing Yuan can be counted in days."

sentences.zh: 」雨霽，懿乃合圍，作土山地道，楯櫓鉤沖，晝夜攻之，矢石如雨。

translations.literal: " When the rain cleared, Yi then closed the encirclement, raised earthworks and dug tunnels, set shields, mantlets, hooks, and rams, and attacked day and night; arrows and stones fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: When the rain cleared, Yi closed the encirclement, raised earthworks and dug tunnels, deployed shields, mantlets, hooks, and rams, and attacked day and night; arrows and stones fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 淵窘急，糧盡，人相食，死者甚多，其將楊祚等降。

translations.literal: Yuan was in dire straits; grain was exhausted; men ate one another; the dead were very many; his generals Yang Zuo and others surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was desperate; grain ran out; men ate one another; the dead were countless; his generals Yang Zuo and others surrendered.

sentences.zh: 八月，淵使相國王建、御史大夫柳甫請解圍卻兵，當君臣面縛。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Yuan sent Chancellor Wang Jian and Grand Censor Liu Fu to beg that the siege be lifted and the army withdrawn, promising that ruler and ministers would bind themselves with faces bared.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Yuan sent Chancellor Wang Jian and Grand Censor Liu Fu to beg that the siege be lifted and the army withdrawn, promising that ruler and ministers would surrender with faces bared.

sentences.zh: 懿命斬之，檄告淵曰：「楚、鄭列國，而鄭伯猶肉袒牽羊迎之。

translations.literal: Yi ordered them beheaded and announced to Yuan by proclamation: "Chu and Zheng were coequal states, yet the Earl of Zheng still bared his flesh and led a sheep to meet the victor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ordered them beheaded and announced to Yuan by proclamation, "Chu and Zheng were coequal states, yet the Earl of Zheng still bared his flesh and led a sheep to meet the victor.

sentences.zh: 孤天子上公，而建等欲孤解圍退捨，豈得禮邪！

translations.literal: I am the Son of Heaven's chief minister—yet Jian and the rest wish me to lift the siege and withdraw. Is that proper ritual!
translations.idiomatic: I am the Son of Heaven's chief minister—yet Jian and the rest wish me to lift the siege and withdraw. Is that proper ritual!

sentences.zh: 二人老耄，傳言失指，已相為斬之。

translations.literal: The two men are old and senile and misstated the message—I have already beheaded them for you.
translations.idiomatic: The two men are old and senile and misstated the message—I have already beheaded them for you.

sentences.zh: 若意有未已，可更遣年少有明決者來！

translations.literal: If your intent is not yet satisfied, you may send younger men with clear resolve!"
translations.idiomatic: If your intent is not yet satisfied, send younger men with clear resolve!"

sentences.zh: 」淵復遣侍中衛演乞剋日送任，懿謂演曰：「軍事大要有五：能戰當戰，不能戰當守，不能守當走；

translations.literal: " Yuan again sent Palace Attendant Wei Yan to beg a set day for delivering hostages. Yi told Yan: "The great essentials of military affairs are five: if you can fight, fight; if you cannot fight, hold; if you cannot hold, flee;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan again sent Palace Attendant Wei Yan to beg a set day for delivering hostages. Yi told Yan, "The great essentials of military affairs are five: if you can fight, fight; if you cannot fight, hold; if you cannot hold, flee;

sentences.zh: 餘二事，但有降與死耳。

translations.literal: of the remaining two matters, there are only surrender and death.
translations.idiomatic: of the remaining two options, there are only surrender and death.

sentences.zh: 汝不肯面縛，此為決就死也，不須送任！

translations.literal: You refuse to bind yourselves with faces bared—this means you have resolved on death; hostages are not needed!"
translations.idiomatic: You refuse to surrender with faces bared—this means you have resolved on death; hostages are not needed!"

sentences.zh: 」任午，襄平潰，淵與子修將數百騎突圍東南走，大兵急擊之，斬淵父子於梁水之上。

translations.literal: " On day Renwu, Xiangping collapsed. Yuan and his son Xiu led several hundred horsemen to break out toward the southeast and flee; the great army pressed the attack and beheaded Yuan and his son on the Liang River.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu, Xiangping fell. Yuan and his son Xiu led several hundred horsemen to break out southeast; the main army pressed the attack and beheaded Yuan and his son on the Liang River.

sentences.zh: 懿既入城，誅其公卿以下及兵民七千餘人，築為京觀。

translations.literal: After Yi entered the city, he executed the ministers and below and soldiers and civilians—more than seven thousand—and built them into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi entered the city, he executed officials and commoners alike—more than seven thousand—and built them into a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 遼東、帶方、樂浪、玄菟四郡皆平。

translations.literal: The four commanderies of Liaodong, Daifang, Lelang, and Xuantu were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The four commanderies of Liaodong, Daifang, Lelang, and Xuantu were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 淵之將反也，將軍綸直、賈范等苦諫，淵皆殺之，懿乃封直等之墓，顯其遺嗣，釋淵叔父恭之囚。

translations.literal: When Yuan was about to rebel, Generals Lun Zhi, Jia Fan, and others admonished him bitterly; Yuan killed them all. Yi then sealed the tombs of Zhi and the rest, honored their surviving heirs, and released Yuan's uncle Gong from prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan was about to rebel, Generals Lun Zhi, Jia Fan, and others admonished him bitterly; Yuan killed them all. Yi then sealed the tombs of Zhi and the rest, honored their surviving heirs, and released Yuan's uncle Gong from prison.

sentences.zh: 中國人欲還舊鄉者，恣聽之。

translations.literal: For subjects of the Central States who wished to return to their old homelands, he allowed it as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: For subjects of the Central States who wished to return to their old homelands, he allowed it as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 遂班師。

translations.literal: He then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 初，淵兄晃為恭任子在洛陽，先淵未反時，數陳其變，欲令國家討淵；

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuan's elder brother Huang was a hostage of Gong in Luoyang. Before Yuan had rebelled, he had repeatedly reported his brother's intentions, wishing the state to campaign against Yuan;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuan's elder brother Huang was a hostage in Luoyang. Before Yuan rebelled, Huang had repeatedly reported his brother's intentions, urging the state to campaign against Yuan;

sentences.zh: 及淵謀逆，帝不忍市斬，欲就獄殺之。

translations.literal: when Yuan plotted rebellion, the Emperor could not bear to execute him in the marketplace and wished to kill him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: when Yuan plotted rebellion, the emperor could not bear to execute Huang in the marketplace and wished to kill him in prison.

sentences.zh: 廷尉高柔上疏曰：「臣竊聞晃先數自歸，陳淵禍萌，雖為凶族，原心可恕。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Gao Rou submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that Huang repeatedly came forward on his own, reporting the budding disaster of Yuan. Though of a criminal clan, his original intent may be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Gao Rou submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that Huang repeatedly came forward on his own, reporting Yuan's budding treason. Though of a criminal clan, his original intent may be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 夫仲尼亮司馬牛之憂，祁奚明叔向之過，在昔之美義也。

translations.literal: Confucius made clear Sima Niu's distress; Qi Xi made plain Shu Xiang's fault—beautiful righteousness of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius made clear Sima Niu's distress; Qi Xi made plain Shu Xiang's fault—beautiful righteousness of former ages.

sentences.zh: 臣以為晃信有言，宜貸其死；

translations.literal: I hold that if Huang's words are believed, his death should be spared;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that if Huang's words are believed, his death should be spared;

sentences.zh: 苟自無言，便當市斬。

translations.literal: if on his own he had said nothing, then he should be executed in the marketplace."
translations.idiomatic: if he had said nothing on his own, then he should be executed in the marketplace."

sentences.zh: 今進不赦其命，退不彰其罪，閉著囹圄，使自引分，四方觀國，或疑此舉也。

translations.literal: Now if in advancing you do not spare his life, yet in retreating you do not make his guilt clear, but shut him in prison and let him take his own life, the four quarters watching the state may doubt this course."
translations.idiomatic: Now if you advance yet do not spare his life, and retreat yet do not make his guilt clear, but shut him in prison and let him take his own life, the four quarters watching the state may doubt this course."

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽，竟遣使繼金屑飲晃及其妻子，賜以棺衣，殯斂於宅。

translations.literal: " The Emperor would not listen and finally sent envoys to follow with gold filings for Huang and his wife and children to drink; he granted coffin and garments and had them buried from the residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen and finally sent envoys with gold filings for Huang and his wife and children to drink; he granted coffin and garments and had them buried from their residence.

sentences.zh: 九月，吳改元赤烏。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wu changed the era name to Chiwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Wu changed the era name to Chiwu.

sentences.zh: 吳步夫人卒。

translations.literal: Lady Bu of Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bu of Wu died.

sentences.zh: 初，吳主為討虜將軍，在吳，娶吳郡徐氏。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Lord of Wu was General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and was in Wu, he married the Xu clan of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Wu ruler was General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and stationed in Wu, he married a woman of the Xu clan of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 太子登所生庶賤，吳主令徐氏母養之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Deng was born of a lowborn concubine; the Lord of Wu ordered Lady Xu to rear him as a mother.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Deng was born of a lowborn concubine; the Wu ruler ordered Lady Xu to rear him as a mother.

sentences.zh: 徐氏妒，故無寵。

translations.literal: Lady Xu was jealous and therefore had no favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu was jealous and therefore won no favor.

sentences.zh: 及吳主西徙，徐氏留處吳。

translations.literal: When the Lord of Wu moved west, Lady Xu remained in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu ruler moved west, Lady Xu remained in Wu.

sentences.zh: 而臨淮步夫人寵冠後庭，吳主欲立為皇后，而群臣議在徐氏，吳主依違者十餘年。

translations.literal: But Lady Bu of Linhuai's favor crowned the rear palace; the Lord of Wu wished to install her as empress, yet the officials argued for the Xu clan, and the Lord of Wu wavered for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: But Lady Bu of Linhuai's favor crowned the rear palace; the Wu ruler wished to install her as empress, yet the officials argued for the Xu clan, and he wavered for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 會步氏卒，群臣奏追贈皇后印綬，徐氏竟廢，卒於吳。

translations.literal: When Lady Bu died, the officials memorialized to posthumously grant empress seals and cords; Lady Xu was finally set aside and died in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Bu died, the officials memorialized to posthumously grant her empress seals and cords; Lady Xu was finally set aside and died in Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳主使中書郎呂壹典校諸官府及州郡文書，壹因此漸作威福，深文巧詆，排陷無辜，毀短大臣，纖介必聞。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu sent Palace Gentleman Lü Yi to supervise and audit the documents of all government offices and commandery and prefecture administrations. Yi thereby gradually wielded power and favor, twisting the law with crafty slander, framing the innocent, and defaming great ministers—no trifle escaped his ear.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler sent Palace Gentleman Lü Yi to audit documents in all government offices and commanderies and prefectures. Yi thereby gradually wielded power and favor, twisting the law with crafty slander, framing the innocent, and defaming great ministers—no trifle escaped his ear.

sentences.zh: 太子登數諫，吳主不聽，群臣莫敢復言，皆畏之側目。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Deng admonished him repeatedly; the Lord of Wu would not listen. The officials dared speak no more and all feared him, watching sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Deng admonished him repeatedly; the Wu ruler would not listen. The officials dared speak no more and all feared Yi, watching sidelong.

sentences.zh: 壹誣白故江夏太守刁嘉謗訕國政，吳主怒，收嘉，繫獄驗問。

translations.literal: Yi falsely reported that the former Administrator of Jiangxia Diao Jia had slandered state affairs. The Lord of Wu was angry, seized Jia, and imprisoned him for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Yi falsely reported that the former Administrator of Jiangxia Diao Jia had slandered state affairs. The Wu ruler was angry, seized Jia, and imprisoned him for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 時同坐人皆怖畏壹，並言聞之。

translations.literal: At the time all who sat together in the case feared Yi and alike said they had heard it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all who sat together in the case feared Yi and alike said they had heard it.

sentences.zh: 侍中北海是儀獨雲無聞，遂見窮詰累日，詔旨轉厲，群臣為之屏息。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Shi Yi of Beihai alone said he had not heard it; he was then pressed with interrogation for many days, the imperial orders growing harsher, and the officials held their breath for him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Shi Yi of Beihai alone said he had not heard it; he was then pressed with interrogation for many days, the imperial orders growing harsher, and the officials held their breath for him.

sentences.zh: 儀曰：「今刀鋸已在臣頸，臣何敢為嘉隱諱，自取夷滅，為不忠之鬼！

translations.literal: Yi said: "Now knife and saw are already at my neck—how dare I conceal and cover for Jia, bringing extinction on myself and becoming an unfaithful ghost!
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Now knife and saw are already at my neck—how dare I conceal and cover for Jia, bringing extinction on myself and becoming an unfaithful ghost!

sentences.zh: 厄以聞知當有本末。

translations.literal: If I claim to have heard, there must be a beginning and end to it.
translations.idiomatic: If I claim to have heard, there must be a beginning and end to it.

sentences.zh: 」據實答問，辭不傾移，吳主遂捨之；

translations.literal: " He answered the questions according to fact, his words not shifting; the Lord of Wu then released him;
translations.idiomatic: He answered according to fact, his words not shifting; the Wu ruler then released him;

sentences.zh: 嘉亦得免。

translations.literal: Jia also escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Jia also escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 上大將軍陸遜、太常潘濬憂壹亂國，每言之，輒流涕。

translations.literal: Grand General Lu Xun and Minister of Ceremonies Pan Jun feared Yi would throw the state into disorder; whenever they spoke of it, tears would flow.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Lu Xun and Minister of Ceremonies Pan Jun feared Yi would throw the state into disorder; whenever they spoke of it, tears would flow.

sentences.zh: 壹白丞相顧雍過失，吳主怒，詰責雍。

translations.literal: Yi reported Chancellor Gu Yong's faults. The Lord of Wu was angry and rebuked Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reported Chancellor Gu Yong's faults. The Wu ruler was angry and rebuked Yong.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎謝肱語次問壹：「顧公事何如？

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Xie Gong, in the course of conversation, asked Yi: "How stands Chancellor Gu's case?
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Xie Gong, in the course of conversation, asked Yi, "How stands Chancellor Gu's case?

sentences.zh: 」壹曰：「不能佳。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Not good.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Not good.

sentences.zh: 」肱又問：「若此公免退，誰當代之？

translations.literal: " Gong asked again: "If this lord is dismissed, who should replace him?
translations.idiomatic: Gong asked again, "If he is dismissed, who should replace him?

sentences.zh: 」壹未答。

translations.literal: " Yi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yi did not answer.

sentences.zh: 肱曰：「得無潘太常得之乎？

translations.literal: Gong said: "Could it be that Minister Pan would get it?
translations.idiomatic: Gong said, "Could it be that Minister Pan would get it?

sentences.zh: 」壹良久曰：「君語近之也。

translations.literal: " After a long while Yi said: "Your words are close to it.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Yi said, "Your words are close to it.

sentences.zh: 」肱曰：「潘太常常切齒於君，但道無因耳。

translations.literal: " Gong said: "Minister Pan constantly gnashes his teeth at you—only that he has had no opening.
translations.idiomatic: Gong said, "Minister Pan constantly gnashes his teeth at you—only that he has had no opening.

sentences.zh: 今日代顧公，恐明日便擊君矣！

translations.literal: If he replaces Chancellor Gu today, I fear tomorrow he will strike at you!
translations.idiomatic: If he replaces Chancellor Gu today, I fear tomorrow he will strike at you!

sentences.zh: 」壹大懼，遂解散雍事。

translations.literal: " Yi was greatly afraid and thereupon dropped the case against Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was greatly afraid and thereupon dropped the case against Yong.

sentences.zh: 潘濬求朝，詣建業，欲盡辭極諫。

translations.literal: Pan Jun requested an audience and went to Jianye, wishing to speak his utmost in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jun requested an audience and went to Jianye, wishing to speak his utmost in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 至，聞太子登已數言之而不見從，濬乃大請百寮，欲因會手刃殺壹，以身當之，為國除患。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he heard the heir Deng had already spoken many times without being heeded. Jun then invited all the hundred officials on a grand scale, wishing at the gathering to kill Yi with his own hand, taking the consequences on himself to remove the state's scourge.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he heard Crown Prince Deng had already spoken many times without being heeded. Jun then invited all the hundred officials on a grand scale, wishing at the gathering to kill Yi with his own hand, taking the consequences on himself to remove the state's scourge.

sentences.zh: 壹密聞知，稱疾不行。

translations.literal: Yi secretly heard of it and pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yi secretly heard of it and pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 西陵督步騭上疏曰：「顧雍、陸遜、潘濬，志在竭誠，寢食不寧，念欲安國利民，建久長之計，可謂心膂股肱社稷之臣矣。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Xiling Bu Zhi submitted a memorial saying: "Gu Yong, Lu Xun, and Pan Jun aim at exhausting sincerity; they cannot rest in sleep or eating, thinking to secure the state and benefit the people and establish a long-lasting plan—they may be called the heart, spine, thigh, and arm ministers of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of Xiling Bu Zhi submitted a memorial saying, "Gu Yong, Lu Xun, and Pan Jun aim at exhausting sincerity; they cannot rest in sleep or eating, thinking to secure the state and benefit the people and establish a long-lasting plan—they may be called the heart, spine, thigh, and arm ministers of the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 宜各委任，不使他官監其所司，課其殿最。

translations.literal: Each should be entrusted with his charge and not have other officials supervise what they administer and grade their performance.
translations.idiomatic: Each should be entrusted with his charge and not have other officials supervise what they administer and grade their performance.

sentences.zh: 此三臣思慮不到則已，豈敢欺負所天乎！

translations.literal: If these three ministers' thoughts fall short, that is all—but how would they dare deceive and wrong their Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: If these three ministers' thoughts fall short, that is all—but how would they dare deceive and wrong their sovereign!"

sentences.zh: 」左將軍朱據部曲應受三萬緡，工王遂詐而受之。

translations.literal: " Left General Zhu Ju's troops were due to receive thirty thousand strings of cash; artisan Wang Sui fraudulently received it.
translations.idiomatic: Left General Zhu Ju's troops were due to receive thirty thousand strings of cash; artisan Wang Sui fraudulently received it.

sentences.zh: 壹疑據實取，考問主者，死於杖下；

translations.literal: Yi suspected Ju had actually taken it and interrogated the responsible clerk, who died under the staff;
translations.idiomatic: Yi suspected Ju had actually taken it and interrogated the responsible clerk, who died under the staff;

sentences.zh: 據哀其無辜，厚棺斂之，壹又表據吏為據隱，故厚其殯。

translations.literal: Ju pitied his innocence and gave him a thick coffin burial. Yi again memorialized that Ju's clerk had concealed for Ju, hence the lavish funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Ju pitied his innocence and gave him a thick coffin burial. Yi again memorialized that Ju's clerk had concealed for Ju, hence the lavish funeral.

sentences.zh: 吳主數責問據，據無以自明，藉草待罪；

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu repeatedly rebuked and questioned Ju; Ju had no way to clear himself and spread grass to await punishment;
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler repeatedly rebuked and questioned Ju; Ju had no way to clear himself and spread grass to await punishment;

sentences.zh: 數日，典軍吏劉助覺，言王遂所取。

translations.literal: after several days, Army Commandant's clerk Liu Zhu discovered it and reported that Wang Sui had taken it.
translations.idiomatic: after several days, Army Commandant's clerk Liu Zhu discovered it and reported that Wang Sui had taken it.

sentences.zh: 吳主大感寤，曰：「朱據見枉，況吏民乎！

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu was greatly awakened and said: "Zhu Ju was wronged—how much more officials and commoners!
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler was greatly awakened and said, "Zhu Ju was wronged—how much more officials and commoners!

sentences.zh: 」乃窮治壹罪，賞助百萬。

translations.literal: " He then exhaustively prosecuted Yi's crimes and rewarded Zhu with a million.
translations.idiomatic: He then exhaustively prosecuted Yi's crimes and rewarded Zhu with a million.

sentences.zh: 丞相雍至廷尉斷獄，壹以囚見。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yong went to the Minister of Justice to try the case; Yi was brought in as a prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yong went to the Minister of Justice to try the case; Yi was brought in as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 雍和顏色問其辭狀，臨出，又謂壹曰：「君意得無慾有所道乎？

translations.literal: Yong with gentle countenance asked about his statements; as he was leaving, he again said to Yi: "Sir, do you perhaps wish to say something?
translations.idiomatic: Yong with gentle countenance asked about his statements; as he was leaving, he again said to Yi, "Sir, do you perhaps wish to say something?

sentences.zh: 」壹叩頭無言。

translations.literal: " Yi kowtowed and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi kowtowed and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 時尚書郎懷敘面詈辱壹，雍責敘曰：「官有正法，何至於此！

translations.literal: At the time Master of Writing Gentleman Huai Xu reviled and insulted Yi to his face. Yong rebuked Xu: "Offices have proper law—how reach to this!
translations.idiomatic: At the time Master of Writing Gentleman Huai Xu reviled and insulted Yi to his face. Yong rebuked Xu, "Offices have proper law—how reach to this!

sentences.zh: 」有司奏壹大辟，或以為宜加焚裂，用彰元惡。

translations.literal: " The responsible offices memorialized the death penalty for Yi; some held that burning and rending should be added to display the arch-villain.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized the death penalty for Yi; some held that burning and rending should be added to display the arch-villain.

sentences.zh: 吳主以訪中書令會稽闞澤，澤曰：「盛明之世，不宜復有此刑。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu consulted Director of the Palace Secretariat Kan Ze of Kuaiji. Ze said: "In an age of flourishing brilliance, this punishment should not be revived."
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler consulted Director of the Palace Secretariat Kan Ze of Kuaiji. Ze said, "In an age of flourishing brilliance, this punishment should not be revived."

sentences.zh: 」吳主從之。

translations.literal: " The Lord of Wu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 壹既伏誅，吳主使中書郎袁禮告謝諸大將，因問時事所當損益。

translations.literal: After Yi had been executed, the Lord of Wu sent Palace Gentleman Yuan Li to announce thanks to the great generals and inquire what in current affairs should be reduced or increased.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi had been executed, the Wu ruler sent Palace Gentleman Yuan Li to announce thanks to the great generals and inquire what in current affairs should be reduced or increased.

sentences.zh: 禮還，復有詔責諸葛瑾、步騭、朱然、呂岱等曰：「袁禮還云：『與子瑜、子山、義封、定公相見，並咨以時事當有所先後，各自以不掌民事，不肯便有所陳，悉推之伯言、承明。

translations.literal: When Li returned, there was again an edict rebuking Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, Zhu Ran, Lü Dai, and the rest, saying: "Yuan Li reports on his return: 'I met Ziyu, Zishan, Yifeng, and Dinggong and consulted them on what in current affairs should come first or last. Each, on the ground that he does not administer civil affairs, was unwilling to speak forthwith and all pushed it onto Boyan and Chengming.
translations.idiomatic: When Li returned, there was again an edict rebuking Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, Zhu Ran, Lü Dai, and the rest, saying, "Yuan Li reports on his return: 'I met Ziyu, Zishan, Yifeng, and Dinggong and consulted them on what in current affairs should come first or last. Each, on the ground that he does not administer civil affairs, was unwilling to speak forthwith and all pushed it onto Boyan and Chengming.

sentences.zh: 伯言、承明見禮，泣涕懇惻，辭旨辛苦，至乃懷執危怖，有不自安之心。

translations.literal: Boyan and Chengming, meeting Li, wept with earnest grief; their words were bitter in intent, even to holding fear of peril and a heart not at ease.'
translations.idiomatic: Boyan and Chengming, meeting Li, wept with earnest grief; their words were bitter in intent, even to holding fear of peril and a heart not at ease.'

sentences.zh: 』聞之悵然，深自刻怪！

translations.literal: ' Hearing this I am desolate and deeply blame myself!
translations.idiomatic: ' Hearing this I am desolate and deeply blame myself!

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 夫惟聖人能無過行，明者能自見耳。

translations.literal: Only the sage can be without wrongful conduct; only the clear-sighted can see himself.
translations.idiomatic: Only the sage can be without wrongful conduct; only the clear-sighted can see himself.

sentences.zh: 人之舉厝，何能悉中！

translations.literal: Men's actions—how can they all hit the mark!
translations.idiomatic: Men's actions—how can they all hit the mark!

sentences.zh: 獨當己有以傷拒眾意，忽不自覺，故諸君有嫌難耳。

translations.literal: I alone must have wounded and rejected the multitude's intent without noticing—hence you gentlemen have grievances and difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: I alone must have wounded and rejected the multitude's intent without noticing—hence you gentlemen have grievances and difficulties.

sentences.zh: 不爾，何緣乃至於此乎」與諸君從事，自少至長，發有二色，以謂表裡足以明露，公私分計足用相保，義雖君臣，恩猶骨肉，榮福喜戚，相與共之。

translations.literal: Otherwise, what cause would bring it to this?' In serving with you gentlemen from youth to age, I have never had two faces; I thought inside and outside were enough to show clearly, public and private accounts enough to protect each other. Though in righteousness we are ruler and minister, in grace we are like bone and flesh; glory, fortune, joy, and sorrow—we share them together.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, what cause would bring it to this?' In serving with you gentlemen from youth to age, I have never had two faces; I thought inside and outside were enough to show clearly, public and private accounts enough to protect each other. Though in righteousness we are ruler and minister, in grace we are like bone and flesh; glory, fortune, joy, and sorrow—we share them together.

sentences.zh: 忠不匿情，智無遺計，事統是非，諸君豈得從容而已哉！

translations.literal: Loyalty does not hide feeling; wisdom leaves no plan behind; affairs turn on right and wrong—how can you gentlemen be at ease and stop there!
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty does not hide feeling; wisdom leaves no plan behind; affairs turn on right and wrong—how can you gentlemen be at ease and stop there!

sentences.zh: 同船濟水，將誰與易！

translations.literal: In the same boat crossing the water—with whom would you exchange places!
translations.idiomatic: In the same boat crossing the water—with whom would you exchange places!

sentences.zh: 齊桓有善，管子未嘗不歎，有過未嘗不諫，諫而不得，終諫不止。

translations.literal: When Duke Huan of Qi had merit, Guan Zhong never failed to praise it; when he had faults, he never failed to remonstrate—and if remonstrance did not succeed, he remonstrated to the end without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Huan of Qi had merit, Guan Zhong never failed to praise it; when he had faults, he never failed to remonstrate—and if remonstrance did not succeed, he remonstrated to the end without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 今孤自省無桓公之德，而諸君諫諍未出於口，仍執嫌難。

translations.literal: Now I examine myself and lack Duke Huan's virtue, yet you gentlemen's remonstrance has not left your mouths and you still hold grievances and difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: Now I examine myself and lack Duke Huan's virtue, yet you gentlemen's remonstrance has not left your mouths and you still hold grievances and difficulties.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，孤於齊桓良優，未知諸君於管子何如耳！

translations.literal: By this reckoning, I am clearly superior to Duke Huan—I do not know how you gentlemen compare to Guan Zhong!
translations.idiomatic: By this reckoning, I am clearly superior to Duke Huan—I do not know how you gentlemen compare to Guan Zhong!

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，壬午，以司空衛臻為司徒，司隸校尉崔林為司空。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, on day Renwu, Minister of Works Wei Zhen was made Minister over the Masses and Director of the Secretariat Cui Lin was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on the day renwu, Minister of Works Wei Zhen was made Minister over the Masses and Director of the Secretariat Cui Lin was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十二月，漢蔣琬出屯漢中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Jiang Wan of Han went out to camp at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Jiang Wan of Shu went out to camp at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，帝不豫。

translations.literal: On day Yichou, the Emperor was unwell.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou, the emperor fell ill.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，立郭夫人為皇后。

translations.literal: On day Xinsi, Lady Guo was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi, Lady Guo was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖為魏公，以贊令劉放、參軍事孫資皆為秘書郎。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Grand Ancestor was Duke of Wei, he made Aide Liu Fang and Staff Officer Sun Zi both Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Grand Ancestor was Duke of Wei, he made Aide Liu Fang and Staff Officer Sun Zi both Secretaries.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，更命秘書曰中書，以放為監，資為令，遂掌機密。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, the Secretariat was renamed the Palace Secretariat; Fang was made Supervisor and Zi Director, and they thereupon held confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, the Secretariat was renamed the Palace Secretariat; Fang was made Supervisor and Zi Director, and they thereupon held confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，尤見寵任，皆加侍中、光祿大夫，封本縣侯。

translations.literal: When the present Emperor took the throne, they were especially favored and entrusted; both were added as Palace Attendants and Household Grandees and enfeoffed as marquises of their native counties.
translations.idiomatic: When the present emperor took the throne, they were especially favored and entrusted; both were added as Palace Attendants and Household Grandees and enfeoffed as marquises of their native counties.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝親覽萬機，數興軍旅，腹心之任，皆二人管之；

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor personally handled the myriad affairs and frequently raised armies; the charge of heart and belly was all managed by the two men;
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor personally handled the myriad affairs and frequently raised armies; the charge of heart and belly was all managed by the two men;

sentences.zh: 每有大事，朝臣會議，常令決其是非，擇而行之。

translations.literal: whenever there was a great matter and the court officials met in council, he regularly had them decide right and wrong and choose what to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: whenever there was a great matter and the court officials met in council, he regularly had them decide right and wrong and choose what to carry out.

sentences.zh: 中護軍蔣濟上疏曰：「臣聞大臣太重者國危，左右太親者身蔽，古之至戒也。

translations.literal: Central Protector of the Army Jiang Ji submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that when great ministers are too weighty the state is endangered, and when those at one's side are too intimate the person is obscured—the utmost warning of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Central Protector of the Army Jiang Ji submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that when great ministers are too weighty the state is endangered, and when those at one's side are too intimate the person is obscured—the utmost warning of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 往者大臣秉事，外內扇動；

translations.literal: In the past great ministers held affairs and inner and outer were stirred;
translations.idiomatic: In the past great ministers held affairs and inner and outer were stirred;

sentences.zh: 陛下卓然自覽萬機，莫不祗肅。

translations.literal: Your Majesty stood forth alone to view the myriad affairs himself, and none were not reverent and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty stood forth alone to view the myriad affairs himself, and none were not reverent and stern.

sentences.zh: 夫大臣非不忠也，然威權在下，則眾心慢上，勢之常也。

translations.literal: Great ministers are not disloyal, yet when authority and power rest below, the multitude's hearts slight the ruler above—this is the constant tendency of circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers are not disloyal, yet when authority and power rest below, the multitude's hearts slight the ruler above—this is the constant tendency of circumstances.

sentences.zh: 陛下既已察之於大臣，願無忘於左右。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already discerned this in great ministers—I pray you not forget it in those at your side.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already discerned this in great ministers—I pray you not forget it in those at your side.

sentences.zh: 左右忠正遠慮，未必賢於大臣，至於便辟取合，或能工之。

translations.literal: Those at the side, loyal and upright with far-reaching thought, are not necessarily more worthy than great ministers; but in ingratiating compliance they may excel at it.
translations.idiomatic: Those at the side, loyal and upright with far-reaching thought, are not necessarily more worthy than great ministers; but in ingratiating compliance they may excel at it.

sentences.zh: 今外所言，輒雲中書。

translations.literal: Now what is spoken outside always says 'the Palace Secretariat.'
translations.idiomatic: Now what is spoken outside always says 'the Palace Secretariat.'

sentences.zh: 雖使恭慎，不敢外交，但有此名，猶惑世俗。

translations.literal: Even if they are made respectful and cautious and dare not deal outside, merely having this name still confuses the worldly.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they are made respectful and cautious and dare not deal outside, merely having this name still confuses the worldly.

sentences.zh: 況實握事要，日在目前，儻因疲倦之間，有所割制，眾臣見其能推移於事，即亦因時而向之。

translations.literal: How much more when they actually grasp the essentials of affairs, day by day before the eyes—if perchance in a moment of weariness they make some cut or control, the officials seeing they can shift matters will also turn toward them as the time suits.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when they actually grasp the essentials of affairs, day by day before the eyes—if perchance in a moment of weariness they make some cut or control, the officials seeing they can shift matters will also turn toward them as the time suits.

sentences.zh: 一有此端，私招朋援，臧否毀譽，必有所興，功負賞罰，必有所易，直道而上者或壅，曲附左右者反達，因微而入，緣形而出，意所狎信，不復猜覺。

translations.literal: Once this beginning exists, they privately recruit partisans; praise and blame, ruin and praise, are sure to arise; merit and fault, reward and punishment, are sure to change; those on the straight path upward may be blocked, while those who crookedly attach to the side reach success instead—entering through the subtle, emerging along the form; those the mind favors and trusts are no longer suspected or perceived.
translations.idiomatic: Once this beginning exists, they privately recruit partisans; praise and blame, ruin and praise, are sure to arise; merit and fault, reward and punishment, are sure to change; those on the straight path upward may be blocked, while those who crookedly attach to the side reach success instead—entering through the subtle, emerging along the form; those the mind favors and trusts are no longer suspected or perceived.

sentences.zh: 此宜聖智所當早聞，外以經意，則形際自見；

translations.literal: This is what sage wisdom should hear early; attend to it from without and the form and boundary will show themselves;
translations.idiomatic: This is what sage wisdom should hear early; attend to it from without and the form and boundary will show themselves;

sentences.zh: 或恐朝臣畏言不合而受左右之怨，莫適以聞。

translations.literal: perhaps the court officials fear that words not agreeing will bring the side's resentment and none dare report it.
translations.idiomatic: perhaps the court officials fear that words not agreeing will bring the side's resentment and none dare report it.

sentences.zh: 臣竊亮陛下潛神默思，公聽並觀，若事有未盡於理而物有未周於用，將改曲易調，遠與黃、唐角功，近昭武、文之績，豈牽近習而已哉！

translations.literal: I privately trust that Your Majesty ponders in hidden spirit and silent thought, listens publicly and views together—if affairs have not exhausted reason or things have not rounded utility, you will change the tune and alter the key, vie in merit with Huangdi and Yao afar and display nearby the achievements of Martial Emperor and Emperor Wen—how would you be bound to near habits alone!
translations.idiomatic: I privately trust that Your Majesty ponders in hidden spirit and silent thought, listens publicly and views together—if affairs have not exhausted reason or things have not rounded utility, you will change the tune and alter the key, vie in merit with Huangdi and Yao afar and display nearby the achievements of Martial Emperor and Emperor Wen—how would you be bound to near habits alone!

sentences.zh: 然人君不可悉任天下之事，必當有所付；

translations.literal: Yet the ruler cannot entirely entrust all under Heaven's affairs—there must be some delegation;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ruler cannot entirely entrust all under Heaven's affairs—there must be some delegation;

sentences.zh: 若委之一臣，自非周公旦之忠，管夷吾之公，則有弄機敗官之敝。

translations.literal: if entrusted to a single minister, unless it be the loyalty of Duke of Zhou Dan or the fairness of Guan Yiwu, there is the harm of manipulating the mechanism and ruining office.
translations.idiomatic: if entrusted to a single minister, unless it be the loyalty of Duke of Zhou Dan or the fairness of Guan Yiwu, there is the harm of manipulating the mechanism and ruining office.

sentences.zh: 當今柱石之士雖少，至於行稱一州，智效一官，忠信竭命，各奉其職，可並驅策，不使聖明之朝有專吏之名也！

translations.literal: Today's pillar-and-stone men are few, yet as to conduct praised in a province, wisdom effective in an office, loyalty and faith exhausting life, each holding his post—they can be driven together and not let a sage-bright court have the name of a monopoly official!"
translations.idiomatic: Today's pillar-and-stone men are few, yet as to conduct praised in a province, wisdom effective in an office, loyalty and faith exhausting life, each holding his post—they can be driven together and not let a sage-bright court have the name of a monopoly official!"

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及寢疾，深念後事，乃以武帝子燕王宇為大將軍，與領軍將軍夏侯獻、武衛將軍曹爽、屯騎校尉曹肇、驍騎將軍秦朗等對輔政。

translations.literal: When he lay ill in bed, deeply considering affairs after death, he then made Martial Emperor's son Prince of Yan Cao Yu Grand General, with General of the Gentlemen of the Household for the Encampments Xiahou Xian, General of the Martial Guard Cao Shuang, Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry Cao Zhao, General of Resolute Cavalry Qin Lang, and others to assist in government facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: When he lay ill in bed, deeply considering affairs after death, he then made Martial Emperor's son Prince of Yan Cao Yu Grand General, with General of the Gentlemen of the Household for the Encampments Xiahou Xian, General of the Martial Guard Cao Shuang, Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry Cao Zhao, General of Resolute Cavalry Qin Lang, and others to assist in government jointly.

sentences.zh: 爽，真之子；

translations.literal: Shuang was Zhen's son;
translations.idiomatic: Shuang was Zhen's son;

sentences.zh: 肇，休之子也。

translations.literal: Zhao was Xiu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was Xiu's son.

sentences.zh: 帝少與燕王宇善，故以後事屬之。

translations.literal: The Emperor from youth was on good terms with Prince of Yan Yu, and therefore entrusted the later affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor from youth was on good terms with Prince of Yan Yu, and therefore entrusted the later affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 劉放、孫資久典機任，獻、肇心內不平；

translations.literal: Liu Fang and Sun Zi had long held confidential charge; Xian and Zhao were inwardly displeased;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang and Sun Zi had long held confidential charge; Xian and Zhao were inwardly displeased;

sentences.zh: 殿中有雞棲樹，二人相謂曰：「此亦久矣，其能復幾！

translations.literal: in the hall there was a tree where chickens roosted. The two men said to each other: "This too has been long—how much longer can it last!
translations.idiomatic: in the hall there was a tree where chickens roosted. The two men said to each other, "This too has been long—how much longer can it last!

sentences.zh: 」放、資懼有後害，陰圖間之。

translations.literal: " Fang and Zi feared later harm and secretly plotted to drive them apart.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Zi feared later harm and secretly plotted to drive them apart.

sentences.zh: 燕王性恭良，陳誠固辭。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was by nature respectful and good and with sincere words firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan was by nature respectful and good and with sincere words firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 帝引放、資入臥內，問曰：「燕王正爾為？

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Fang and Zi into the sickroom and asked: "Is the Prince of Yan really like this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Fang and Zi into the sickroom and asked, "Is the Prince of Yan really like this?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「燕王實自知不堪大任故耳。

translations.literal: " They replied: "The Prince of Yan truly knows himself unfit for a great charge—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "The Prince of Yan truly knows himself unfit for a great charge—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「誰可任者？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Who can be entrusted?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Who can be entrusted?

sentences.zh: 」時惟曹爽獨在帝側，放、資因薦爽，且言：「宜召司馬懿與相參。

translations.literal: " At the time only Cao Shuang was alone at the Emperor's side. Fang and Zi thereupon recommended Shuang and also said: "Sima Yi should be summoned to share in government."
translations.idiomatic: At the time only Cao Shuang stood at the emperor's side. Fang and Zi recommended Shuang and also said, "Sima Yi should be summoned to share in government."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「爽堪其事不？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Is Shuang equal to the task?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Is Shuang equal to the task?

sentences.zh: 」爽流汗不能對。

translations.literal: " Shuang sweated and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang sweated and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 放躡其足，耳之曰：「臣以死奉社稷。

translations.literal: Fang trod on his foot and whispered in his ear: "I will with my death serve the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Fang trod on his foot and whispered in his ear, "I will with my death serve the altars of soil and grain."

sentences.zh: 」帝從放、資言，欲用爽、懿，既而中變，敕停前命；

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed Fang and Zi's words and wished to employ Shuang and Yi; then he changed his mind midway and ordered the previous command stopped;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Fang and Zi's words and wished to employ Shuang and Yi; then he changed his mind midway and ordered the previous command stopped;

sentences.zh: 放、資復入見說帝，帝又從之。

translations.literal: Fang and Zi again entered and persuaded the Emperor, and the Emperor again followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Zi again entered and persuaded the emperor, and he again followed them.

sentences.zh: 放曰：「宜為手詔。

translations.literal: Fang said: "There should be a handwritten edict."
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, "There should be a handwritten edict."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我困篤，不能。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "I am gravely ill and cannot."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I am gravely ill and cannot."

sentences.zh: 」放即上床，執帝手強作之，遂繼出，大言曰：「有詔免燕王宇等官，不得停省中。

translations.literal: " Fang at once mounted the bed, seized the Emperor's hand and forced the writing, then followed out and proclaimed loudly: "There is an edict dismissing Prince of Yan Yu and the rest from office—they may not remain in the inner palace."
translations.idiomatic: Fang at once mounted the bed, seized the emperor's hand and forced the writing, then followed out and proclaimed loudly, "There is an edict dismissing Prince of Yan Yu and the rest from office—they may not remain in the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 」皆流涕而出。

translations.literal: " All wept as they went out.
translations.idiomatic: All wept as they went out.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以曹爽為大將軍。

translations.literal: On day Jiashen, Cao Shuang was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen, Cao Shuang was made Grand General.

sentences.zh: 帝嫌爽才弱，復拜尚書孫禮為大將軍長史以佐之。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought Shuang's talent weak and again appointed Master of Writing Sun Li as the Grand General's Chief Clerk to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Shuang's talent weak and again appointed Master of Writing Sun Li as the Grand General's Chief Clerk to assist him.

sentences.zh: 是時，司馬懿在汲，帝令給使辟邪繼手詔召之。

translations.literal: At this time Sima Yi was at Ji; the Emperor ordered attendant Bixie to follow with the handwritten edict summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Sima Yi was at Ji; the emperor ordered attendant Bixie to follow with the handwritten edict summoning him.

sentences.zh: 先是，燕王為帝畫計，以為關中事重，宜遣懿便道自軹關西還長安，事已施行。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Prince of Yan had drawn up a plan for the Emperor, holding that Guanzhong affairs were weighty and Yi should be sent by a convenient route from Zhiguan west back to Chang'an; the matter had already been put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Prince of Yan had drawn up a plan for the emperor, holding that Guanzhong affairs were weighty and Yi should be sent by a convenient route from Zhiguan west back to Chang'an; the matter had already been put into effect.

sentences.zh: 懿斯須得二詔，前後相違，疑京師有變，乃疾驅入朝。

translations.literal: Yi in a moment received two edicts that contradicted each other before and after; he suspected change in the capital and thereupon galloped in haste to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yi in a moment received two edicts that contradicted each other; he suspected change in the capital and galloped in haste to court.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝下景初三年（

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, lower scroll, Jingchu year three (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Three (conclusion), Jingchu year 3 (

sentences.zh: 己未，公元二三九年）

translations.literal: Jiwei, the year 239 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: jiwei cycle, AD 239)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，懿至，入見，帝執其手曰：「吾以後事屬君，君與曹爽輔少子。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Yi arrived and entered audience. The Emperor grasped his hand and said: "I entrust the later affairs to you—you and Cao Shuang shall assist the young son.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Yi arrived and entered audience. The emperor grasped his hand and said, "I entrust the later affairs to you—you and Cao Shuang shall assist the young son.

sentences.zh: 死乃可忍，吾忍死待君，得相見，無所復恨矣！

translations.literal: Death alone can be borne; I bore death awaiting you—now that we meet, there is nothing more to regret!
translations.idiomatic: Death alone can be borne; I bore death awaiting you—now that we meet, there is nothing more to regret!

sentences.zh: 」乃召齊、秦二王以示懿，別指齊王芳謂懿曰：「此是也，君諦視之，勿誤也！

translations.literal: " He then summoned the Princes of Qi and Qin to show Yi, and separately pointing to Prince of Qi Fang said to Yi: "This is he—look closely and do not mistake!
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the Princes of Qi and Qin to show Yi, and separately pointing to Prince of Qi Fang said to Yi, "This is he—look closely and do not mistake!

sentences.zh: 」又教齊王令前抱懿頸。

translations.literal: " He also instructed the Prince of Qi to come forward and embrace Yi's neck.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed the Prince of Qi to come forward and embrace Yi's neck.

sentences.zh: 懿頓首流涕。

translations.literal: Yi knocked his head and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Yi knocked his head and wept.

sentences.zh: 是日，立齊王為皇太子。

translations.literal: That day the Prince of Qi was installed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Prince of Qi was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝尋殂。

translations.literal: The Emperor soon died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon died.

sentences.zh: 帝沈毅明敏，任心而行，料簡功能，屏絕浮偽。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deep, resolute, bright, and keen; he acted as his heart directed, weighed and selected ability, and barred out floating falsity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deep, resolute, bright, and keen; he acted as his heart directed, weighed and selected ability, and barred out floating falsity.

sentences.zh: 行師動眾，論決大事，謀臣將相，鹹服帝之大略。

translations.literal: In marching armies and moving the multitude, in debating and deciding great affairs, strategists, generals, and ministers—all submitted to the Emperor's grand design.
translations.idiomatic: In marching armies and moving the multitude, in debating and deciding great affairs, strategists, generals, and ministers—all submitted to the emperor's grand design.

sentences.zh: 性特強識，雖左右小臣，官簿性行，名跡所履，及其父兄子弟，一經耳目，終不遺忘。

translations.literal: His nature was especially strong in memory: even petty officials at his side—their office registers, nature and conduct, names and tracks trodden, and their fathers, brothers, and sons—once they passed ear or eye, he never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was especially strong in memory: even petty officials at his side—their office registers, nature and conduct, names and tracks trodden, and their fathers, brothers, and sons—once they passed ear or eye, he never forgot.

sentences.zh: 孫盛論曰：聞之長老，魏明帝天姿秀出，立發垂地，口吃少言，而沈毅好斷。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng's commentary says: Hearing from elders, Emperor Ming of Wei had heaven's talent standing forth, hair standing to the ground when erect, stammering and few words, yet deep, resolute, and fond of decision.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's commentary says: Hearing from elders, Emperor Ming of Wei had heaven's talent standing forth, hair standing to the ground when erect, stammering and few words, yet deep, resolute, and fond of decision.

sentences.zh: 初，諸公受遺輔導，帝皆以方任處之，政自己出。

translations.literal: At first the lords received the testament to assist and guide, but the Emperor all placed them in square posts of responsibility; government issued from himself.
translations.idiomatic: At first the lords received the testament to assist and guide, but the emperor all placed them in square posts of responsibility; government issued from himself.

sentences.zh: 優禮大臣，開容善直，雖犯顏極諫，無所摧戮，其君人之量如此之偉也。

translations.literal: He honored great ministers with preferential rites, opened his countenance to good straight speech—even when they offended his face with extreme remonstrance, there was no crushing or killing; his measure as ruler of men was thus grand.
translations.idiomatic: He honored great ministers with preferential rites, opened his countenance to good straight speech—even when they offended his face with extreme remonstrance, there was no crushing or killing; his measure as ruler of men was thus grand.

sentences.zh: 然不思建德垂風，不固維城之基，至使大權偏據，社稷無衛，悲夫！

translations.literal: Yet he did not think to establish virtue and let the wind hang down, did not solidify the foundation of the protecting walls, until great power lay one-sided and the altars of soil and grain had no guard—how sad!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he did not think to establish virtue and let the wind hang down, did not solidify the foundation of the protecting walls, until great power lay one-sided and the altars of soil and grain had no guard—how sad!

sentences.zh: 太子即位，年八歲；

translations.literal: The heir apparent took the throne at age eight;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took the throne at age eight;

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后曰皇太后，加曹爽、司馬懿侍中，假節鉞，都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The empress was honored as empress dowager; Cao Shuang and Sima Yi were added as Palace Attendants, loaned staffs of authority and axes, made Directors of all armies inner and outer, and Recorders of Palace Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was honored as empress dowager; Cao Shuang and Sima Yi were added as Palace Attendants, loaned staffs of authority and axes, made Directors of all armies inner and outer, and Recorders of Palace Secretariat Affairs.

sentences.zh: 諸所興作宮室之役，皆以遺詔罷之。

translations.literal: All labor for palace construction that had been undertaken was stopped by testamentary edict.
translations.idiomatic: All labor for palace construction that had been undertaken was stopped by testamentary edict.

sentences.zh: 爽、懿各領兵三千人更宿殿內，爽以懿年位素高，常父事之，每事咨訪，不敢專行。

translations.literal: Shuang and Yi each led three thousand troops in rotation to lodge within the hall. Shuang, because Yi's age and rank had always been high, regularly served him as a father, consulting on every matter and not daring to act alone.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang and Yi each led three thousand troops in rotation to lodge within the hall. Shuang, because Yi's age and rank had always been high, regularly served him as a father, consulting on every matter and not daring to act alone.

sentences.zh: 初，并州刺史東平畢軌及鄧颺、李勝、何晏、丁謐皆有才名而急於富貴，趨時附勢，明帝惡其浮華，皆抑而不用。

translations.literal: Earlier, Inspector of Bing Province Bi Gui of Dongping and Deng Yang, Li Sheng, He Yan, and Ding Mi all had reputations for talent yet were eager for wealth and rank, courting the times and attaching to power. Emperor Ming hated their superficial show and all suppressed them without employing them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Inspector of Bing Province Bi Gui of Dongping and Deng Yang, Li Sheng, He Yan, and Ding Mi all had reputations for talent yet were eager for wealth and rank, courting the times and attaching to power. Emperor Ming hated their superficial show and all suppressed them without employing them.

sentences.zh: 曹爽素與親善，及輔政，驟加引擢，以為腹心。

translations.literal: Cao Shuang had long been on intimate terms with them; when he assisted in government he suddenly promoted them and made them his heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang had long been on intimate terms with them; when he assisted in government he suddenly promoted them and made them his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 晏，進之孫；

translations.literal: Yan was Jin's grandson;
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Jin's grandson;

sentences.zh: 謐，斐之子也。

translations.literal: Mi was Fei's son.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was Fei's son.

sentences.zh: 晏等鹹共推戴爽，以為重權不可委於人。

translations.literal: Yan and the rest all together urged Shuang forward, holding that heavy power could not be entrusted to another man.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the rest all urged Shuang forward, holding that heavy power could not be entrusted to another man.

sentences.zh: 丁謐為爽畫策，使爽白天子發詔，轉司馬懿為太傅，外以名號尊之，內欲令尚書奏事，先來由己，得制其輕重也。

translations.literal: Ding Mi drew up a plan for Shuang, having Shuang tell the Son of Heaven to issue an edict transferring Sima Yi to Grand Tutor—outwardly honoring him with a title, inwardly wishing that when the Masters of Writing reported affairs they should first come through himself so he could control their weight.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Mi drew up a plan for Shuang, having Shuang tell the Son of Heaven to issue an edict transferring Sima Yi to Grand Tutor—outwardly honoring him with a title, inwardly wishing that when the Masters of Writing reported affairs they should first come through himself so he could control their weight.
