sentences.zh: 爽從之。

translations.literal: Shuang followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang followed this.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁丑，以司馬懿為太傅，以爽弟羲為中領軍，訓為武衛將軍，彥為散騎常侍、侍講，其餘諸弟皆以列侯侍從，出入禁闥，貴寵莫盛焉。

translations.literal: In the second month, on day Dingchou, Sima Yi was made Grand Tutor; Shuang's younger brother Xi was made Central Commander of the Gentlemen of the Household; Xun was made General of the Martial Guard; Yan was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Lecturer-in-Attendance; the rest of the younger brothers all attended as ranked marquises, entering and leaving the forbidden gates—none were more honored and favored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day dingchou, Sima Yi was made Grand Tutor; Shuang's younger brother Xi was made Central Commander of the Gentlemen of the Household; Xun was made General of the Martial Guard; Yan was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Lecturer-in-Attendance; the rest of the younger brothers all attended as ranked marquises, entering and leaving the forbidden gates—none were more honored and favored.

sentences.zh: 爽事太傅，禮貌雖存，而諸所興造，希復由之。

translations.literal: Shuang served the Grand Tutor; courtesy and ritual remained, yet undertakings rarely again passed through him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang served the Grand Tutor; courtesy and ritual remained, yet undertakings rarely again passed through him.

sentences.zh: 爽徙吏部尚書盧毓為僕射，而以何晏代之，以鄧颺、丁謐為尚書，畢軌為司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Shuang moved Minister of the Civil Service Lu Yu to Vice Minister and replaced him with He Yan; made Deng Yang and Ding Mi Masters of Writing; and Bi Gui Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang moved Minister of the Civil Service Lu Yu to Vice Minister and replaced him with He Yan; made Deng Yang and Ding Mi Masters of Writing; and Bi Gui Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晏等依勢用事，附會者升進，違忤者罷退，內外望風，莫敢忤旨。

translations.literal: Yan and the rest relied on power to wield affairs; those who attached were promoted, those who opposed were dismissed; inner and outer watched the wind and none dared oppose the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the rest relied on power to wield affairs; those who attached were promoted, those who opposed were dismissed; inner and outer watched the wind and none dared oppose the intent.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎傅嘏謂爽弟羲曰：「何平叔外靜而內躁，銛巧好利，不念務本，吾恐必先惑子兄弟，仁人將遠而朝政廢矣！

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Fu Gu said to Shuang's younger brother Xi: "He Pingshu is outwardly calm yet inwardly restless, sharp and crafty, fond of profit, not mindful of attending to fundamentals—I fear he will first bewilder you brothers, humane men will withdraw, and court government will be abandoned!
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Fu Gu said to Shuang's younger brother Xi, "He Pingshu is outwardly calm yet inwardly restless, sharp and crafty, fond of profit, not mindful of attending to fundamentals—I fear he will first bewilder you brothers, humane men will withdraw, and court government will be abandoned!

sentences.zh: 」晏等遂與嘏不平，因微事免嘏官。

translations.literal: " Yan and the rest thereupon were displeased with Gu and on a petty matter dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the rest thereupon were displeased with Gu and on a petty matter dismissed him from office.

sentences.zh: 又出盧毓為廷尉，畢軌又枉奏毓免官，眾論多訟之，乃復以為光祿勳。

translations.literal: Lu Yu was again sent out as Minister of Justice; Bi Gui again falsely memorialized to dismiss Yu from office; public opinion largely pleaded for him, and he was again made Household Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu was again sent out as Minister of Justice; Bi Gui again falsely memorialized to dismiss Yu from office; public opinion largely pleaded for him, and he was again made Household Grandee.

sentences.zh: 孫禮亮直不撓，爽心不便，出為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Sun Li was bright and straight and unbending; Shuang found it inconvenient at heart and sent him out as Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Li was bright and straight and unbending; Shuang found it inconvenient at heart and sent him out as Inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 三月，以征東將軍滿寵為太尉。

translations.literal: In the third month, General Who Campaigns East Man Chong was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, General Who Campaigns East Man Chong was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，吳督軍使者羊道擊遼東守將，俘人民而去。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Wu's Army Supervisor Envoy Yang Dao attacked Liaodong's defending general, captured the people, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Wu's Army Supervisor Envoy Yang Dao attacked Liaodong's defending general, captured the people, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 漢蔣琬為大司馬，東曹掾犍為楊戲，素性簡略，琬與言論，時不應答。

translations.literal: In Han, Jiang Wan was Grand Marshal; Eastern Bureau Aide Yang Xi of Jianwei was by nature brief and simple—when Wan spoke with him in discussion, he sometimes did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu, Jiang Wan was Grand Marshal; Eastern Bureau Aide Yang Xi of Jianwei was by nature brief and simple—when Wan spoke with him in discussion, he sometimes did not answer.

sentences.zh: 或謂琬曰：「公與戲語而不應，其慢甚矣！

translations.literal: Someone said to Wan: "You speak with Xi and he does not answer—his rudeness is extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Wan, "You speak with Xi and he does not answer—his rudeness is extreme!

sentences.zh: 」琬曰：「人心不同，各如其面，面從後言，古人所誡。

translations.literal: " Wan said: "Hearts differ, each like its face; to agree to the face and speak otherwise behind—this the ancients warned against.
translations.idiomatic: Wan said, "Hearts differ, each like its face; to agree to the face and speak otherwise behind—this the ancients warned against.

sentences.zh: 戲欲贊吾是邪，則非其本心；

translations.literal: If Xi wished to praise me as right, that would not be his true heart;
translations.idiomatic: If Xi wished to praise me as right, that would not be his true heart;

sentences.zh: 欲反吾言，則顯吾之非，是以默然，是戲之快也。

translations.literal: if he wished to oppose my words, that would display my wrong—hence his silence; that is Xi's pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: if he wished to oppose my words, that would display my wrong—hence his silence; that is Xi's pleasure."

sentences.zh: 又督農楊敏；

translations.literal: Also Agricultural Supervisor Yang Min—
translations.idiomatic: Also Agricultural Supervisor Yang Min—

sentences.zh: 敏嘗毀琬曰：「作事憒憒，誠不及前人。

translations.literal: Min once slandered Wan, saying: "In doing affairs he is muddled—truly he does not reach his predecessors.
translations.idiomatic: Min once slandered Wan, saying, "In doing affairs he is muddled—truly he does not reach his predecessors.

sentences.zh: 」或以白琬，主者請推治敏，琬曰：「吾實不如前人，無可推也。

translations.literal: " Someone reported this to Wan; the responsible official asked to pursue and punish Min. Wan said: "I truly do not reach my predecessors—there is nothing to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported this to Wan; the responsible official asked to pursue and punish Min. Wan said, "I truly do not reach my predecessors—there is nothing to pursue.

sentences.zh: 」主者乞問其憒憒之狀，琬曰：「苟其不如，則事不理，事不理，則憒憒矣。

translations.literal: " The official begged to ask the form of his muddling. Wan said: "If he is not equal, then affairs are not ordered; if affairs are not ordered, then there is muddling."
translations.idiomatic: The official begged to ask the form of his muddling. Wan said, "If he is not equal, then affairs are not ordered; if affairs are not ordered, then there is muddling."

sentences.zh: 」後敏坐事繫獄，眾人猶懼其必死，琬心無適莫，敏得免重罪。

translations.literal: " Later Min was imprisoned for an offense; the crowd still feared he would surely die, but Wan's heart had no near or far, and Min escaped heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Later Min was imprisoned for an offense; the crowd still feared he would surely die, but Wan's heart had no near or far, and Min escaped heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，帝始親臨朝。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the Emperor began personally to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the emperor began personally to attend court.

sentences.zh: 八月，大赦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，吳太常潘濬卒。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Wu's Minister of Ceremonies Pan Jun died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Wu's Minister of Ceremonies Pan Jun died.

sentences.zh: 吳主以鎮南將軍呂岱代濬，與陸遜共領荊州文書。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu made General Who Pacifies the South Lü Dai replace Jun, and with Lu Xun jointly oversaw Jing Province documents.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler made General Who Pacifies the South Lü Dai replace Jun, and with Lu Xun jointly oversaw Jing Province documents.

sentences.zh: 岱時年已八十，體素精勤，躬親王事，與遜同心協規，有善相讓，南士稱之。

translations.literal: Dai was then already eighty; his person was by nature refined and diligent, personally attending to royal affairs; with Xun he shared one heart and coordinated plans, yielding good to each other—the southern gentlemen praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Dai was then already eighty; his person was by nature refined and diligent, personally attending to royal affairs; with Xun he shared one heart and coordinated plans, yielding good to each other—the southern gentlemen praised them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，吳將廖式殺臨賀太守嚴綱等，自稱平南將軍，攻零陵、桂陽，搖動交州諸郡，眾數萬人，呂岱自表輒行，星夜兼路，吳主遣使追拜交州牧，及遣諸將唐咨等絡繹相繼，攻討一年，破之，斬式及其支黨，郡縣悉平。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wu general Liao Shi killed Administrator of Linhe Yan Gang and others, styled himself General Who Pacifies the South, attacked Lingling and Guiyang, and shook the commanderies of Jiaozhou—his host numbered tens of thousands. Lü Dai memorialized on his own authority to go at once, traveling day and night by double marches; the Lord of Wu sent envoys to confer on him retroactively the post of Governor of Jiaozhou and dispatched generals Tang Zi and others in continuous succession; after a year of attack and suppression they broke them, beheaded Shi and his branch and party, and commanderies and counties were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Wu general Liao Shi killed Administrator of Linhe Yan Gang and others, styled himself General Who Pacifies the South, attacked Lingling and Guiyang, and shook the commanderies of Jiaozhou—his host numbered tens of thousands. Lü Dai memorialized on his own authority to go at once, traveling day and night by double marches; the Wu ruler sent envoys to confer on him retroactively the post of Governor of Jiaozhou and dispatched generals Tang Zi and others in continuous succession; after a year of attack and suppression they broke them, beheaded Shi and his branch and party, and commanderies and counties were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 岱復還武昌。

translations.literal: Dai again returned to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai again returned to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 吳都鄉侯周胤將兵千人屯公安，有罪，徙廬陵；

translations.literal: Wu Marquis of the Capital District Zhou Yin led a thousand troops garrisoned at Gong'an; he had guilt and was moved to Luling;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Marquis of the Capital District Zhou Yin led a thousand troops garrisoned at Gong'an; he had guilt and was moved to Luling;

sentences.zh: 諸葛瑾、步騭為之請。

translations.literal: Zhuge Jin and Bu Zhi pleaded for him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Jin and Bu Zhi pleaded for him.

sentences.zh: 吳主曰：「昔胤年少，初無功勞，橫受精兵，爵以侯將，蓋念公瑾以及於胤也。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu said: "In the past Yin was young and at first had no merit or labor, yet was given elite troops in excess and ennobled marquis-general—this was thinking of Gongjin and extending it to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler said, "In the past Yin was young and at first had no merit or labor, yet was given elite troops in excess and ennobled marquis-general—this was thinking of Gongjin and extending it to Yin.

sentences.zh: 而胤恃此，酗淫自恣，前後告諭，曾無悛改。

translations.literal: Yet Yin relied on this, drunk and dissolute, indulging himself; warnings before and after never brought repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yin relied on this, drunk and dissolute, indulging himself; warnings before and after never brought repentance.

sentences.zh: 孤於公瑾，義猶二君，樂胤成就，豈有已哉！

translations.literal: I toward Gongjin in righteousness am like two lords; I delight in Yin's accomplishment—how could there be an end!
translations.idiomatic: I toward Gongjin in righteousness am like two lords; I delight in Yin's accomplishment—how could there be an end!

sentences.zh: 迫胤罪惡，未宜便還，且欲苦之，使自知耳。

translations.literal: Pressed by Yin's crimes and wickedness, it is not yet fitting to return him at once—I wish rather to distress him so he may know himself.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by Yin's crimes and wickedness, it is not yet fitting to return him at once—I wish rather to distress him so he may know himself.

sentences.zh: 以公瑾之子，而二君在中間，苟使能改，亦何患乎！

translations.literal: As Gongjin's son, with you two lords in the middle—if he can reform, what is there to fear!
translations.idiomatic: As Gongjin's son, with you two lords in the middle—if he can reform, what is there to fear!

sentences.zh: 」瑜兄子偏將軍峻卒，全琮請使峻子護領其兵。

translations.literal: " Yu's elder brother's son Partial General Jun died; Quan Cong asked that Jun's son Hu lead his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's elder brother's son Partial General Jun died; Quan Cong asked that Jun's son Hu lead his troops.

sentences.zh: 吳主曰：「昔走曹操，拓有荊州，皆是公瑾，常不忘之。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu said: "In the past we routed Cao Cao and expanded to hold Jing Province—all was Gongjin; I never forget it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler said, "In the past we routed Cao Cao and expanded to hold Jing Province—all was Gongjin; I never forget it.

sentences.zh: 初聞峻亡，仍欲用護。

translations.literal: When I first heard Jun had died, I still wished to employ Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When I first heard Jun had died, I still wished to employ Hu.

sentences.zh: 聞護性行危險，用之適為作禍，故更止之。

translations.literal: Hearing Hu's nature and conduct were perilous, employing him would precisely make disaster—so I stopped again.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Hu's nature and conduct were perilous, employing him would precisely make disaster—so I stopped again.

sentences.zh: 孤念公瑾，豈有已哉！

translations.literal: I think of Gongjin—how could there be an end!
translations.idiomatic: I think of Gongjin—how could there be an end!

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔復以建寅之月為正。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict restored the first month as jianyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, an edict restored the first month as jianyin.

sentences.zh: 邵陵厲公上

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Shaoling, Part One

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝下正始元年（

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, lower scroll, Zhengshi year one (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Three (conclusion), Zhengshi year 1 (

sentences.zh: 庚申，公元二四零年）

translations.literal: Gengshen, the year 240 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: gengshen cycle, AD 240)

sentences.zh: 春，旱。

translations.literal: Spring: drought.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, drought.

sentences.zh: 越巂蠻夷數叛漢，殺太守，是後太守不敢之郡，寄治安定縣，去郡八縣餘里。

translations.literal: The barbarians of Yuexi repeatedly rebelled against Han and killed the administrator; thereafter the administrator dared not go to the commandery seat and lodged government at Anding county, more than eight counties' distance from the seat.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians of Yuexi repeatedly rebelled against Han and killed the administrator; thereafter the administrator dared not go to the commandery seat and lodged government at Anding county, more than eight counties' distance from the seat.

sentences.zh: 漢主以巴西張嶷為越巂太守，嶷招慰新附，誅討強猾，蠻夷畏服，郡界悉平，復還舊治。

translations.literal: The Han ruler made Zhang Ni of Baxi Administrator of Yuexi. Ni comforted the newly attached, punished and attacked the strong and cunning; the barbarians feared and submitted, the commandery borders were all pacified, and he returned to the old seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu emperor made Zhang Ni of Baxi Administrator of Yuexi. Ni comforted the newly attached, punished and attacked the strong and cunning; the barbarians feared and submitted, the commandery borders were all pacified, and he returned to the old seat of government.

sentences.zh: 冬，吳饑。

translations.literal: Winter: Wu suffered famine.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Wu suffered famine.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝下正始二年（

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, lower scroll, Zhengshi year two (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Three (conclusion), Zhengshi year 2 (

sentences.zh: 辛酉，公元二四一年）

translations.literal: Xinyou, the year 241 of the Common Era)
translations.idiomatic: xinyou cycle, AD 241)

sentences.zh: 春，吳人將伐魏。

translations.literal: Spring: the men of Wu were about to campaign against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the men of Wu were about to campaign against Wei.

sentences.zh: 零陵太守殷札言於吳主曰：「今天棄曹氏，喪誅累見，虎爭之際而幼童蒞事。

translations.literal: Administrator of Lingling Yin Zha said to the Lord of Wu: "Now Heaven has abandoned the Cao clan; mourning and executions appear in succession—it is the moment of tigers contending while a young child holds affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Lingling Yin Zha said to the Wu ruler, "Now Heaven has abandoned the Cao clan; mourning and executions appear in succession—it is the moment of tigers contending while a young child holds affairs.

sentences.zh: 陛下身自御戎，取亂侮亡，宜滌荊、揚之地，舉強羸之數，使強者執戟，羸者轉運。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should personally take the army, seize disorder and insult the perishing; you should cleanse the lands of Jing and Yang, raise the count of strong and weak, let the strong bear halberds and the weak transport supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should personally take the army, seize disorder and insult the perishing; you should cleanse the lands of Jing and Yang, raise the count of strong and weak, let the strong bear halberds and the weak transport supplies.

sentences.zh: 西命益州，軍於隴右，授諸葛瑾、朱然大眾，直指襄陽，陸遜、朱桓別征壽春，大駕入淮陽，歷青、徐。

translations.literal: Command Yizhou in the west to army on Longyou's right; give Zhuge Jin and Zhu Ran great hosts pointing straight at Xiangyang; Lu Xun and Zhu Huan separately campaign Shouchun; the imperial carriage enters Huaiyang and passes through Qing and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Command Yizhou in the west to army on Longyou's right; give Zhuge Jin and Zhu Ran great hosts pointing straight at Xiangyang; Lu Xun and Zhu Huan separately campaign Shouchun; the imperial carriage enters Huaiyang and passes through Qing and Xu.

sentences.zh: 襄陽、壽春，困於受敵，長安以西，務御蜀軍，許、洛之眾，勢必分離，掎角並進，民必內應。

translations.literal: Xiangyang and Shouchun, trapped by receiving attack on both sides; west of Chang'an they must focus on defending against Shu armies; the masses at Xu and Luoyang will necessarily be divided; with pincers advancing together, the people will surely respond from within.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiangyang and Shouchun beset on every side, Wei must hold Chang'an's western flank against Shu while splitting Xu and Luoyang's strength; advance in coordinated pincers and the populace will rise within.

sentences.zh: 將帥對向，或失便宜，一軍敗績，則三軍離心。

translations.literal: When generals face each other, they may miss what is expedient; if one army meets defeat, then the three armies lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: Rival commanders may each miss the opportune move; one routed column and the whole campaign loses cohesion.

sentences.zh: 便當秣馬脂車，陵蹈城邑，乘勝逐北，以定華夏。

translations.literal: Then one should feed horses and grease chariots, tread over walled cities, ride victory in pursuit northward, and thereby settle Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: Then harness the army, storm the cities, press the fleeing foe, and secure the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 若不悉軍動眾，循前輕舉，則不足大用，易於屢退，民疲威消，時往力竭，非上策也。

translations.literal: If one does not fully mobilize the army and masses but follows the former light enterprises, then it is insufficient for great use, easy to retreat repeatedly; the people grow weary, prestige dissolves, time passes and strength is exhausted—this is not the superior strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Without full mobilization, repeating half-hearted sorties wastes the moment: repeated withdrawals exhaust the people and erode authority until strength fails—that is no winning policy.

sentences.zh: 」吳主不能用。

translations.literal: " The Lord of Wu could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Wu ruler would not adopt the plan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，吳全琮略淮南，決芍陂，諸葛恪攻六安，朱然圍樊，諸葛瑾攻柤中。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Wu's Quan Cong raided Huainan, breached Quepi Dam, Zhuge Ke attacked Liu'an, Zhu Ran besieged Fan, and Zhuge Jin attacked Zhazhong.
translations.idiomatic: In summer's fourth month Wu forces struck on several fronts: Quan Cong raided Huainan and broke Quepi's dam, Zhuge Ke assailed Liu'an, Zhu Ran invested Fan, and Zhuge Jin marched on Zhazhong.

sentences.zh: 征東將軍王凌、揚州刺史孫禮與全琮戰於芍陂，琮敗走。

translations.literal: Campaign Eastern General Wang Ling and Yangzhou Inspector Sun Li fought Quan Cong at Quepi; Cong was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign Eastern General Wang Ling and Yangzhou inspector Sun Li met Quan Cong at Quepi and drove him off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史胡質以輕兵救樊，或曰：「賊盛，不可迫。

translations.literal: Jingzhou Inspector Hu Zhi with light troops rescued Fan; someone said: "The bandits are numerous—one must not press close.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou inspector Hu Zhi hurried light forces to Fan's relief; advisers warned, "The enemy is too strong to close with.

sentences.zh: 」質曰：「樊城卑兵少，故當進軍為之外援，不然，危矣。

translations.literal: " Zhi said: "Fan City is low and its soldiers few, so I ought to advance and serve as outer support; otherwise it is perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhi replied, "Fan is low-walled and undermanned—I must march to relieve it from outside; otherwise it will fall.

sentences.zh: 」遂勒兵臨圍，城中乃安。

translations.literal: " He thereupon led troops to the siege perimeter, and within the city they were then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed to the siege lines, and the defenders' alarm subsided.

sentences.zh: 五月，吳太子登卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Wu crown prince Deng died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Wu heir apparent Deng died.

sentences.zh: 吳兵猶在荊州，太傅懿曰：「柤中民夷十萬，隔在水南，流離無主，樊城被攻，歷月不解，此危事也，請自討之。

translations.literal: Wu troops were still in Jingzhou; Grand Tutor Yi said: "At Zhazhong a hundred thousand Han and tribal people lie south of the water, displaced and without a lord; Fan City has been under attack a full month unresolved—this is a perilous matter; I ask to go and subdue it myself.
translations.idiomatic: With Wu still holding Jingzhou, Grand Tutor Sima Yi said, "A hundred thousand folk at Zhazhong south of the river are uprooted and leaderless, and Fan has been besieged a month unresolved—I must lead the relief myself.

sentences.zh: 」六月，太傅懿督諸軍救樊；

translations.literal: " In the sixth month the Grand Tutor Yi oversaw the armies to rescue Fan;
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth month Sima Yi took command and marched to relieve Fan;

sentences.zh: 吳軍聞之，夜遁。

translations.literal: hearing this, the Wu army fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: the Wu force slipped away overnight at the news.

sentences.zh: 追至三州口，大獲而還。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Sanzhou Ford, they gained a great haul and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued to Sanzhou Ford, took rich spoils, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 閏月，吳大將軍諸葛瑾卒。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Wu Grand General Zhuge Jin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Wu grand general Zhuge Jin died.

sentences.zh: 瑾長子恪先已封侯，吳主以恪弟融襲爵，攝兵業，駐公安。

translations.literal: Jin's eldest son Ke had already been enfeoffed as a marquis; the Lord of Wu had Ke's younger brother Rong inherit the title, assume military duties, and station at Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's eldest son Zhuge Ke already held a marquisate; the Wu ruler let his brother Rong succeed the fief, take command, and garrison Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 漢大司馬蔣琬以諸葛亮數出秦川，道險，運糧難，卒無成功。

translations.literal: Han Grand Marshal Jiang Wan, because Zhuge Liang several times went out by Qin River route—the road perilous, transport of grain difficult—ultimately had no success.
translations.idiomatic: Han grand marshal Jiang Wan saw that Zhuge Liang's repeated thrusts up the Qin valley failed on bad roads and crippling supply lines.

sentences.zh: 乃多作舟船，欲乘漢、沔東下，襲魏興、上庸。

translations.literal: He therefore made many boats and ships, intending by riding the Han and Mian eastward to strike Weixing and Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: He built a large fleet instead, planning to descend the Han and Mian to strike Weixing and Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 會舊疾連動，未時得行。

translations.literal: But his old illness flared in succession, and in time he could not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Recurrent illness soon kept him from sailing.

sentences.zh: 漢人鹹以為事有不捷，還路甚難，非長策也，漢主遣尚書令費禕、中監軍姜維等喻指。

translations.literal: Han people all thought the affair would not succeed and the return route very difficult, not a long-term policy; the Han ruler sent Palace Attendant Fei Yi, Central Supervisor of the Army Jiang Wei, and others to convey the point.
translations.idiomatic: Han officials judged the plan unlucky and the withdrawal treacherous, no lasting strategy; the Han ruler sent Fei Yi, Jiang Wei, and others to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 琬乃上言：「今魏跨帶九州，根蒂滋蔓，平除未易。

translations.literal: Wan thereupon submitted a memorial: "Now Wei spans and holds the Nine Provinces; roots and tendrils spread luxuriantly—to level and remove them is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan memorialized, "Wei now grips the nine provinces with spreading roots—uprooting it will not be quick work.

sentences.zh: 若東西並力，首尾掎角，雖未能速得如志，且當分裂蠶食，先摧其支黨。

translations.literal: If east and west exert strength together, head and tail in pincer coordination, though we may not swiftly attain our wish, we should nonetheless split and gnaw away, first crushing their branches and partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if Shu and Wu strike from both ends in a pincer, we can gorge on Wei piecemeal even if victory tarries, nibbling off its limbs first.

sentences.zh: 然吳期二三，連不克果。

translations.literal: Yet Wu's appointed times come two or threefold, and in succession they do not achieve the fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, however, has missed its deadlines again and again and delivered nothing.

sentences.zh: 輒與費禕等議，以涼州胡塞之要，進退有資，且羌、胡乃心思漢如渴，宜以姜維為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: I repeatedly discussed with Fei Yi and others that the chokepoint of Liangzhou's Hu and Di is vital—for advance and retreat there are resources; moreover the Qiang and Hu minds turn toward Han as if thirsty; it is fitting to make Jiang Wei Liangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: I urged Fei Yi and colleagues that Liangzhou's Di and Hu frontier is the pivot for advance and retreat, and those tribes long for Han; appoint Jiang Wei inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 若維征行，御制河右，臣當帥軍為維鎮繼。

translations.literal: If Wei campaigns, controlling the region west of the Yellow River, I shall lead the army to secure his rear.
translations.idiomatic: Let Wei drive on the Hexi; I will follow with the main army to cover his rear.

sentences.zh: 今涪水陸四通，惟急是應，若東北有虞，赴之不難，清徙屯涪。

translations.literal: Now Fu's water and land connect in four directions—only urgency need be answered; if there is alarm in the northeast, hurrying there is not difficult; I beg to move the encampment to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu links by water and road in every direction, ready for any crisis in the northeast; move headquarters to Fu.

sentences.zh: 」漢主從之。

translations.literal: " The Han ruler followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Han ruler agreed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲廣田畜谷於揚、豫之間，使尚書郎汝南鄧艾行陳、項已東至壽春。

translations.literal: The court wished to expand tuntian fields for storing grain between Yang and Yu, and sent Secretariat Gentleman Deng Ai of Runan to inspect from Chen and Xiang eastward to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court sought to enlarge military colonies across Yang and Yu and dispatched Secretariat gentleman Deng Ai from Runan to survey the line from Chen and Xiang east to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 艾以為：「昔太祖破黃巾，因為屯田，積穀許都以制四方。

translations.literal: Ai held: "Formerly the Ancestor defeated the Yellow Turbans and thereby established tuntian, accumulating grain at Xu to control the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai argued, "When the Grand Ancestor broke the Yellow Turbans he founded tuntian, stockpiling grain at Xu to dominate all quarters.

sentences.zh: 今三隅已定，事在淮南，每大軍出征，運兵過半，功費巨億。

translations.literal: Now the three corners are settled; the matter lies in Huainan; each time the great army goes forth, transport troops exceed half the host, cost and toil mount to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: With three fronts pacified the contest has shifted to Huainan, yet every major expedition still spends more than half its strength hauling supplies at staggering cost.

sentences.zh: 陳、蔡之間，土下田良，可省許昌左右諸稻田，並水東下，令淮北屯二萬人，淮南三萬人，什二分休，常有四萬人且田且守；

translations.literal: Between Chen and Cai the land is low and fields fertile; one may reduce the paddy fields left and right of Xuchang and, following the water eastward, set twenty thousand men in tuntian north of the Huai and thirty thousand south of it, with one in ten resting by rotation, so that always forty thousand shall both farm and guard;
translations.idiomatic: Between Chen and Cai the soil is rich; shift some Xuchang rice lands east along the waterways, station twenty thousand colonists north of the Huai and thirty thousand south, rotate one tenth off duty, and keep forty thousand farming and guarding at once;

sentences.zh: 益開河渠以增溉灌，通漕運。

translations.literal: further open canals and ditches to increase irrigation, and open grain transport by water.
translations.idiomatic: dig canals for irrigation and open waterborne grain routes.

sentences.zh: 計除眾費，歲完五百萬斛以為軍資，六、七年間，可積三千萬斛於淮上，此則十萬之眾五年食也。

translations.literal: Calculating removal of the masses' expense, each year one may complete five million hu as army stores; in six or seven years one may amass thirty million hu on the Huai—this is then five years' food for a host of a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting convoy costs, the yearly yield could reach five million hu; in six or seven years thirty million hu would sit on the Huai—enough to feed a hundred thousand soldiers for five years.

sentences.zh: 以此乘吳，無不克矣。

translations.literal: With this to strike Wu, there is none that will not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: With that stockpile Wu could not stand.

sentences.zh: 」太傅懿善之。

translations.literal: " Grand Tutor Yi approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Yi endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，始開廣漕渠，每東南有事，大興軍眾，泛舟而下，達於江、淮，資食有儲而無水害。

translations.literal: This year they first broadened the grain transport canal; whenever there was business in the southeast, they greatly raised armies and masses, rode boats downstream, reaching Jiang and Huai, with provisions stored and without water harm.
translations.idiomatic: That year work widened the grain canal; whenever the southeast flared, armies embarked downstream to the Yangtze and Huai with stores laid in and floods checked.

sentences.zh: 管寧卒。

translations.literal: Guan Ning died.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ning died.

sentences.zh: 寧名行高潔，人望之者，邈然若不可及，即之熙熙和易。

translations.literal: Ning's fame for conduct was lofty and pure; those who looked on him from afar seemed beyond reach, yet coming near found him warm and easy.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ning was famed for lofty purity; from afar he seemed unapproachable, yet up close he was genial and accessible.

sentences.zh: 能因事導人於善，人無不化服。

translations.literal: He could, by the matter at hand, lead people toward goodness, and none failed to be transformed and submit.
translations.idiomatic: He guided people to goodness through the occasion at hand, and none left unconvinced.

sentences.zh: 及卒，天下知與不知，聞之無不嗟歎。

translations.literal: At his death, whether they knew him or not, all who heard sighed without exception.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, all who heard—friend and stranger alike—sighed in grief.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝下正始三年（

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, lower scroll, Zhengshi year three (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Three (conclusion), Zhengshi year 3 (

sentences.zh: 壬戌，公元二四二年）

translations.literal: renxu, AD 242)
translations.idiomatic: renxu, AD 242)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，漢姜維率偏軍自漢中還住涪。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Han's Jiang Wei led a detached force from Hanzhong back to garrison at Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in spring Jiang Wei brought a detachment from Hanzhong to Fu.

sentences.zh: 吳主立其子和為太子，大赦。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu installed his son He as crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler named his son He heir apparent and granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 三月，昌邑景侯滿寵卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, Marquis Jing of Changyi Man Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Marquis Jing of Changyi Man Chong died.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙酉，以領軍將軍蔣濟為太尉。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on yiyou, he made Colonel of the Palace Guard Jiang Ji Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn's seventh month, on the day yiyou, Colonel of the Palace Guard Jiang Ji was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 吳主遣將軍聶友、校尉陸凱將兵三萬擊儋耳、珠崖。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu sent General Nie You and Colonel Lu Kai with thirty thousand troops to attack Dan'er and Zhuya.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler sent General Nie You and Colonel Lu Kai with thirty thousand men against Dan'er and Zhuya.

sentences.zh: 八月，吳主封子霸為魯王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Lord of Wu enfeoffed his son Ba as Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Wu ruler enfeoffed his son Ba as Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 霸，和母弟也，寵愛崇特，與和無殊。

translations.literal: Ba, He's younger brother by the same mother, received extraordinary favor, without distinction from He.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was He's uterine brother yet was petted to the same degree as the heir.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射是儀領魯王傅，上疏諫曰：「臣竊以為魯王天挺懿德，兼資文武，當今之宜，宜鎮四方，為國籓輔。

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Masters of Writing Shi Yi as tutor to the Prince of Lu submitted a remonstrance, saying: "Your servant ventures to hold that the Prince of Lu, heaven-endowed with virtue and blessed, combining civil and military gifts, under present circumstances ought to secure the four quarters as a nation's border shield.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Shi Yi, as tutor to the Prince of Lu, memorialized, "I hold that Prince Lu, endowed with virtue and versed in civil and military affairs, should now be posted to guard the realm's frontiers as a royal bulwark.

sentences.zh: 宣揚德美，廣耀威靈，乃國家之良規，海內所瞻望。

translations.literal: Proclaiming and extending virtuous beauty, broadly displaying majesty and spirit, is the state's fine plan and what within the seas looks up to.
translations.idiomatic: Let him spread imperial grace and display martial prestige—that is sound policy and the expectation of the empire.

sentences.zh: 且二宮宜有降殺，以正上下之序，明教化之本。

translations.literal: Moreover the Two Palaces ought to have reductions in rank, to rectify the order of high and low and clarify the root of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two palaces should be kept unequal in rank to preserve hierarchy and the lesson of proper order.

sentences.zh: 」書三、四上，吳主不聽。

translations.literal: " The memorial went up three or four times; the Lord of Wu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent the memorial three or four times; the Wu ruler ignored him.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝下正始四年（

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, lower scroll, Zhengshi year four (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Three (conclusion), Zhengshi year 4 (

sentences.zh: 癸亥，公元二四三年）

translations.literal: guihai, AD 243)
translations.idiomatic: guihai, AD 243)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，帝加元服。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor performed the capping ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In spring's first month the emperor came of age.

sentences.zh: 吳諸葛恪襲六安，掩其人民而去。

translations.literal: Wu Zhuge Ke raided Liu'an, seized its people, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke of Wu raided Liu'an, carried off the population, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，立皇后甄氏，大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, he established Lady Zhen as empress and proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In summer's fourth month he made Lady Zhen empress and amnestied the realm.

sentences.zh: 後，文昭皇后兄儼之孫也。

translations.literal: The empress was granddaughter of Emperor Wen's elder brother Yan's son.
translations.idiomatic: The new empress was granddaughter of Emperor Wen's brother Yan.

sentences.zh: 五月，朔，日有食之，既。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first of the month, there was an eclipse of the sun, total.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth month's new moon a total solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，漢蔣琬自漢中還住涪，疾益甚，以漢中太守王平為前監軍、鎮北大將軍，督漢中。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Han Jiang Wan returned from Hanzhong to garrison at Fu; his illness grew severe, and he made Hanzhong Administrator Wang Ping front Supervisor of the Army and Grand General Who Pacifies the North, overseeing Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In winter's tenth month Jiang Wan came back from Hanzhong to Fu, failing fast; he appointed Wang Ping front army supervisor and Grand General Who Pacifies the North to command Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，漢主以尚書令費禕為大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Han ruler made Palace Attendant Fei Yi Grand General and recorder of Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Han ruler made Fei Yi grand general and coordinator of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 吳丞相顧雍卒。

translations.literal: Wu Chancellor Gu Yong died.
translations.idiomatic: Wu chancellor Gu Yong died.

sentences.zh: 吳諸葛恪遠遣諜人觀相徑要，欲圖壽春。

translations.literal: Wu Zhuge Ke sent spies far to reconnoiter paths and chokepoints, intending to target Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke sent distant scouts to map approaches, plotting against Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 太傅懿將兵入舒，欲以攻恪，吳主徙恪屯於柴桑。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yi led troops into Shu, intending to attack Ke; the Lord of Wu moved Ke's encampment to Chaisang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi marched into Shu to strike Ke, and the Wu ruler shifted Ke's camp to Chaisang.

sentences.zh: 步騭、朱然各上疏於吳主曰：「自蜀還者，鹹言蜀欲背盟，與魏交通，多作舟船，繕治城郭。

translations.literal: Bu Zhi and Zhu Ran each submitted memorials to the Lord of Wu, saying: "Those returning from Shu all say Shu intends to break the alliance and communicate with Wei, making many boats and ships and repairing walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Zhi and Zhu Ran each warned the Wu ruler, "Travelers from Shu report plans to betray the alliance for Wei, with mass shipbuilding and fortification.

sentences.zh: 又，蔣琬守漢中，聞司馬懿南向，不出兵乘虛以掎角之，反委漢中，還近成都。

translations.literal: Moreover Jiang Wan holds Hanzhong; hearing Sima Yi marched south, he did not send troops to seize the void for a pincer; instead he entrusted Hanzhong and returned near Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan remains at Hanzhong yet, hearing Sima Yi marched south, refused a flanking strike and withdrew toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 事已彰灼，無所復疑，宜為之備。

translations.literal: The matter is already blazing clear, without anything further to doubt; preparations should be made.
translations.idiomatic: The signs are plain—doubt is gone; arm against it.

sentences.zh: 」吳主答曰：「吾待蜀不薄，聘享盟誓，無所負之，何以致此！

translations.literal: " The Lord of Wu replied: "I treat Shu not thinly—embassies and oaths of alliance, I have borne nothing against them; how could they come to this!
translations.idiomatic: " The Wu ruler answered, "I have never slighted Shu—embassies and treaties bind us—how could they turn so!

sentences.zh: 司馬懿前來入舒，旬日便退。

translations.literal: Sima Yi came before into Shu and in ten days then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi entered Shu and withdrew within ten days.

sentences.zh: 蜀在萬里，何知緩急而便出兵乎？

translations.literal: Shu is ten thousand li away—how would it know urgency and slackness and then conveniently send troops?
translations.idiomatic: Shu lies ten thousand li off—how could it judge our pace and march out in time?

sentences.zh: 昔魏欲入漢川，此間始嚴，亦未舉動，會聞魏還而止，蜀寧可復以此有疑邪！

translations.literal: Formerly Wei wished to enter Han River region; here we first grew strict, yet also did not move; when we heard Wei had returned we stopped—can Shu again on this account harbor doubt!
translations.idiomatic: When Wei once threatened Hanzhong we stiffened defenses without moving until Wei retreated—why should Shu now suspect us of the same!

sentences.zh: 人言苦不可信，朕為諸君破家保之。

translations.literal: What people say bitterly cannot be believed; I shall for you lords break my house to keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor is treacherous; I will stake my house on their good faith for your sake.

sentences.zh: 征東將軍、都督揚、豫諸軍事王昶上言：「地有常險，守無常勢。

translations.literal: Campaign Eastern General and overseer of Yang and Yu military affairs Wang Chang submitted a memorial, saying: "Terrain has constant peril, but defense has no constant posture.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign Eastern General Wang Chang, overseer of Yang and Yu, memorialized, "Terrain offers fixed advantages, but defense has no fixed posture.

sentences.zh: 今屯宛去襄陽三百餘里，有急不足相赴。

translations.literal: Now the encampment at Wan is more than three hundred li from Xiangyang; if there is urgency it is insufficient to hurry to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Our camp at Wan lies three hundred li from Xiangyang—too far to answer a sudden alarm.

sentences.zh: 」遂徙屯新野。

translations.literal: " He thereupon moved the encampment to Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: " He shifted headquarters to Xinye.

sentences.zh: 宗室曹冏上書曰：「古之王者，必建同姓以明親親，必樹異姓以明賢賢。

translations.literal: A member of the imperial clan, Cao Jiong, submitted a memorial, saying: "The ancient kings must establish men of the same surname to clarify intimacy among kin and must plant men of different surnames to clarify esteem for the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansman Cao Jiong memorialized, "Ancient kings enfeoffed kinsmen to cement blood ties and elevated outsiders to honor merit.

sentences.zh: 親親之道專用，則其漸也微弱；

translations.literal: If the way of cherishing kin is used exclusively, then the gradation is weakness;
translations.idiomatic: Rely only on kin and power thins;

sentences.zh: 賢賢之道偏任，則其敝也劫奪。

translations.literal: if the way of esteeming worthies is one-sidedly entrusted, then the harm is seizure.
translations.idiomatic: lean only on outsiders and usurpation follows.

sentences.zh: 先聖知其然也，故博求親疏而並用之，故能保其社稷，歷經長久。

translations.literal: The former sages knew it would be so; therefore they broadly sought both near and distant kin and employed both together, and so could preserve their altars and states and pass through long duration.
translations.idiomatic: Sages knew this and used kin and outsiders together, keeping state and throne for ages.

sentences.zh: 今魏尊尊之法雖明，親親之道未備，或任而不重，或釋而不任。

translations.literal: Now Wei's law of honoring the honored is clear, but the way of cherishing kin is not complete; some are entrusted but not weighty, or released but not entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei honors rank yet neglects kin-support—some clansmen are named but not empowered, others freed but not trusted.

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟此，寢不安席，謹撰合所聞，論其成敗曰：昔夏、商、周歷世數十，而秦二世而亡。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects on this and cannot rest on mat or pillow, respectfully compiling what he has heard and discussing success and failure, saying: Formerly Xia, Shang, and Zhou passed through dozens of generations, yet Qin in two generations perished.
translations.idiomatic: I brood on this sleeplessly and set out what I know of success and failure: Xia, Shang, and Zhou endured dozens of reigns; Qin collapsed in two.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 三代之君與天下共其民，故天下同其憂；

translations.literal: The rulers of the Three Dynasties shared their people with the realm, so the realm shared their cares;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dynasties' kings shared the people with the realm, so the realm shared their troubles;

sentences.zh: 秦王獨制其民，故傾危而莫救也。

translations.literal: the King of Qin alone controlled his people, so when he toppled none could save him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's king ruled the people alone, and when crisis came none could rescue him.

sentences.zh: 秦觀周之弊，以為小弱見奪，於是廢五等之爵，立郡縣之官，內無宗子以自毘輔，外無諸侯以為籓衛，譬猶芟刈股肱，獨任胸腹。

translations.literal: Qin observed Zhou's defects, holding that small and weak were seized; thereupon it abolished the five ranks of nobility and established commandery-and-county officials, within having no imperial clansmen to support from within, without having no feudal lords as border guards—like mowing off arms and legs and relying on chest and belly alone.
translations.idiomatic: Qin saw Zhou's weakness in petty lords and abolished the five ranks for commanderies and counties, leaving no kin within to brace the throne and no feudal shields without—like cutting off limbs and trusting the torso alone.

sentences.zh: 觀者為之寒心，而始皇晏然自以為子孫帝王萬世之業也，豈不悖哉！

translations.literal: Observers were chilled at heart for it, yet the First Emperor was at ease, himself taking it as his descendants' imperial enterprise for ten thousand generations—was it not perverse!
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers shuddered, yet the First Emperor calmly assumed his line would rule forever—how perverse!

sentences.zh: 故漢祖奮三尺之劍，驅烏集之眾，五年之中，遂成帝業。

translations.literal: Therefore Han's Ancestor wielded a three-foot sword, drove a flock-gathered multitude, and within five years then completed the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Han founder drew his sword, rallied a scattered host, and within five years won the empire.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 伐深根者難為功，摧枯朽者易為力，理勢然也。

translations.literal: To cut down deep roots is hard to achieve merit; to break withered rot is easy to exert force—reason and momentum are so.
translations.idiomatic: Uprooting deep roots is arduous; snapping dry wood is easy—that is the way of things.

sentences.zh: 漢監秦之失，封殖子弟；

translations.literal: Han observed Qin's failure and enfeoffed and nurtured its younger sons;
translations.idiomatic: Han learned from Qin and enfeoffed the imperial house;

sentences.zh: 及諸呂擅權，圖危劉氏，而天下所以不傾動者，徒以諸侯強大，盤石膠固故也。

translations.literal: When the Lü clan monopolized power and plotted peril for the Liu house, the reason the realm did not topple was solely that the feudal lords were strong and bedrock-solid.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lü clan seized power and threatened the Liu throne, the realm held firm only because powerful feudal lords stood like bedrock.

sentences.zh: 然高祖封建，地過古制，故賈誼以為欲天下之治安，莫若眾建諸侯而少其力；

translations.literal: Yet Gaozu's enfeoffment exceeded the ancient system in territory, so Jia Yi held that to desire the realm's peace and order, nothing matched multiplying feudal lords while reducing their strength;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gaozu had granted lands beyond ancient measure, so Jia Yi urged many small feudatories to keep the realm at peace;

sentences.zh: 文帝不從。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 至於孝景，猥用晁錯之計，削黜諸侯，遂有七國之患。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Xiao Jing, he rashly used Chao Cuo's plan, demoting and dismissing feudal lords, and thereupon had the calamity of the Seven States.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jing he rashly adopted Chao Cuo's scheme to strip the princes, provoking the Rebellion of the Seven States.

sentences.zh: 蓋兆發高帝，釁鐘文、景，由寬之過制，急之不漸故也。

translations.literal: The omen issued from Gaozu, the feud flared at Wen and Jing—from leniency's excess in system and urgency's lack of gradualness.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble began with Gaozu's overgenerous grants and erupted under Wen and Jing through lenience followed by sudden harshness.

sentences.zh: 所謂『末大必折，尾大難掉』，尾同於體，猶或不從，況乎非體之尾，其可掉哉！

translations.literal: What is called 'when the tip grows large it must break, when the tail grows large it is hard to wag'—a tail the same as the body may still not obey; how much more a tail not of the body—can it be wagged!
translations.idiomatic: As the saying runs, 'A branch too heavy must snap, a tail too large cannot wag'—even a tail part of the body may refuse command; how much less an alien appendage!

sentences.zh: 武帝從主父之策，下推恩之令，自是之後，遂以陵夷，子孫微弱，衣食租稅，不預政事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu followed Zhufu Yan's policy and issued the decree extending grace; from this onward they declined by degrees, descendants weak and slight, fed by rent and tax, not participating in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu took Zhufu Yan's advice and issued the grace decree; thereafter the feudal lines dwindled, their heirs living on stipends alone, barred from politics.

sentences.zh: 至於哀、平，王氏秉權，假周公之事而為田常之亂，宗室王侯，或乃為之符命，頌莽恩德，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: When it came to Ai and Ping, the Wang clan grasped power, borrowing the deeds of the Duke of Zhou to enact the chaos of Tian Chang; princes and marquises of the imperial clan even made for them talismanic mandates and praised Mang's grace and virtue—is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: By the reigns of Ai and Ping, the Wang clan held power, cloaking usurpation in Zhou Gong's name while acting like Tian Chang; some imperial princes even forged omens and sang Wang Mang's praises—how pitiable!

sentences.zh: 由斯言之，非宗子獨忠孝於惠、文之間而叛逆於哀、平之際也，徒權輕勢弱，不能有定耳。

translations.literal: From this it is said: it was not that clansmen sons alone were loyal and filial between Hui and Wen and rebelled at the time of Ai and Ping; it was merely that power was light and momentum weak, unable to have stability.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that imperial clansmen were not loyal only under Hui and Wen and rebellious only under Ai and Ping; they simply lacked weight and strength to hold the realm steady.

sentences.zh: 賴光武皇帝挺不世之姿，擒王莽於已成，紹漢嗣於既絕，斯豈非宗子之力也！

translations.literal: Relying on Emperor Guangwu's upraised unmatched bearing, he seized Wang Mang when already accomplished and continued Han's succession when already cut off—is this not the power of clansmen sons!
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Emperor Guangwu's unmatched force of character, who seized Wang Mang at the height of his triumph and restored Han when the line seemed dead—was that not the work of the imperial clan!

sentences.zh: 而曾不監秦之失策，襲周之舊制，至於桓、靈，閹宦用事，郡孤立於上，臣弄權於下；

translations.literal: Yet they never took warning from Qin's mistaken policies and followed Zhou's old system; when it reached Huan and Ling, eunuchs handled affairs—the ruler isolated above while ministers toyed with power below;
translations.idiomatic: Yet none took warning from Qin's mistakes or Zhou's example; by Huan and Ling, eunuchs ruled, the throne isolated above while ministers manipulated power below;

sentences.zh: 由是天下鼎沸，奸宄並爭，宗廟焚為灰燼，宮室變為榛藪。

translations.literal: From this the realm boiled like a cauldron, traitors and villains contended together, the ancestral temple burned to ash, and palace halls turned to thicket and scrub.
translations.idiomatic: The empire seethed, traitors and rebels contended, ancestral temples burned to ash, and palace halls reverted to wilderness.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝龍飛鳳翔，掃除凶逆。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor Emperor ascended like a dragon flying and phoenix soaring, sweeping away the vicious and rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor rose like dragon and phoenix, sweeping away the vicious and rebellious.

sentences.zh: 大魏之興，於今二十有四年矣。

translations.literal: Great Wei's rise has now been twenty and four years.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei has now stood for twenty-four years.

sentences.zh: 觀五代之存亡而不用其長策，睹前車之傾覆而不改於轍跡。

translations.literal: They observed the survival and perishing of five reigns yet did not use their long policies; they beheld the overturned cart ahead yet did not alter their wheel tracks.
translations.idiomatic: They watched five dynasties rise and fall yet ignored the lessons; they saw the overturned cart ahead yet would not change course.

sentences.zh: 子弟王空虛之地，君有不使之民；

translations.literal: Younger brothers and sons were enfeoffed kings on empty lands; the ruler had people he could not employ;
translations.idiomatic: Princes held hollow domains while the ruler commanded subjects he could not deploy;

sentences.zh: 宗室竄於閭閻，不聞邦國之政；

translations.literal: The imperial clan hid in alleys and lanes, never hearing the state's government;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan dwelt in ordinary lanes, shut out from statecraft;

sentences.zh: 權均匹夫，勢齊凡庶。

translations.literal: Their authority equaled common fellows; their momentum equaled ordinary folk.
translations.idiomatic: Their power matched any commoner's; their standing equaled ordinary folk.

sentences.zh: 內無深根不拔之固，外無盤石宗盟之助，非所以安社稷，為萬世之業也。

translations.literal: Within they had no deep roots unmoved and unuprooted firmness; without they had no boulder-like clan alliance's aid—this was not the means to settle the altars of soil and grain and make the enterprise of ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Within lay no deep-rooted strength; without lay no bedrock of clan allies—hardly the way to secure the realm for generations.

sentences.zh: 且今之州牧、郡守，古之方伯、諸侯，皆跨有千里之土，兼軍武之任，或比國數人，或兄弟並據；

translations.literal: Moreover today's regional inspectors and commandery administrators, the ancient regional lords and feudal lords, all straddled a thousand li of land and combined civil-military duties; some matched several states in number, some brothers jointly held territory;
translations.idiomatic: Today's provincial governors and prefects are the feudal lords of old, each commanding a thousand li and both civil and military power—some several princes in one region, some brothers sharing command;

sentences.zh: 而宗室子弟曾無一人間廁其間，與相維制，非所以強幹弱枝，備萬一之虞也。

translations.literal: Yet among imperial clansmen's sons and younger brothers not one stood between to balance them and mutually restrain—not the means to strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches, preparing for the one-in-ten-thousand contingency.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no imperial clansman stood among them to balance power—not the way to strengthen the center, weaken the periphery, and guard against disaster.

sentences.zh: 今之用賢，或超為名都之主，或為偏師之帥；

translations.literal: Now in employing the worthy, some were skipped over to become masters of famous capitals, or became commanders of separate armies;
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men today are made masters of great cities or commanders of independent armies;

sentences.zh: 而宗室有文者必限小縣之宰，有武者必致百人之上，非所以勸進賢能、褒異宗室之禮也。

translations.literal: Yet among the imperial clan, those with literary talent were surely limited to magistrates of small counties; those with martial talent were surely sent to command a hundred men or more—this was not the ritual for encouraging and advancing the worthy and talented and honoring and distinguishing the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Literary clansmen were capped at petty county magistrates, martial ones at centurion rank—hardly the ritual to honor merit and elevate the royal house.

sentences.zh: 語曰：『百足之蟲，至死不僵』，以其扶之者眾也。

translations.literal: The saying runs: 'A hundred-foot creature, at death is not stiff,' because those who support it are many.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying runs, "A centipede stiffens only in death because so many legs hold it up."

sentences.zh: 此言雖小，可以譬大。

translations.literal: This saying though small can illustrate the large.
translations.idiomatic: Though a small saying, it illumines a great truth.

sentences.zh: 是以聖王安不忘危，存不忘亡，故天下有變而無傾危之患矣。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage king in security did not forget danger, in existence did not forget perishing; thus when the realm had change there was no peril of overturn and danger.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the sage king, secure, never forgot peril; in prosperity never forgot ruin—so when trouble came, the realm did not topple.

sentences.zh: 」冏冀以此論感寤曹爽，爽不能用。

translations.literal: " Jiong hoped with this argument to awaken Cao Shuang; Shuang could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiong hoped this discourse would move Cao Shuang, but Shuang would not heed it.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝下正始五年（

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, lower scroll, Zhengshi year five (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Three (conclusion), Zhengshi year 5 (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元二四四年）

translations.literal: jiazi cycle, CE two hundred forty-four)
translations.idiomatic: jiazi cycle, AD 244)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，吳主以上大將軍陸遜為丞相，其州牧、都護、領武昌事如故。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Lord of Wu made Superior Grand General Lu Xun Chancellor; his posts as regional inspector, chief protector, and in charge of Wuchang affairs remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Wu ruler made Superior Grand General Lu Xun chancellor while his posts as regional inspector, chief protector, and administrator of Wuchang remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍、都督雍、涼諸軍事夏侯玄，大將軍爽之姑子也。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West, Supervisor of Military Affairs for Yong and Liang, Xiahou Xuan was the Grand General Shuang's nephew by a paternal aunt's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the West Xiahou Xuan, supreme commander on the Yong-Liang frontier, was Grand General Cao Shuang's nephew.

sentences.zh: 玄辟李勝為長史，勝及尚書鄧颺欲令爽立威名於天下，勸使伐蜀；

translations.literal: Xuan recruited Li Sheng as chief clerk; Sheng and Secretariat Director Deng Yang wished to make Shuang establish a reputation and name in the realm and urged him to attack Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan recruited Li Sheng as chief clerk; Sheng and Secretariat Director Deng Yang sought glory for Shuang and urged an invasion of Shu;

sentences.zh: 太傅懿止之，不能得。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yi stopped it but could not obtain his way.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yi opposed it but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 三月，爽西至長安，發卒十餘萬人，與玄自駱谷入漢中。

translations.literal: In the third month, Shuang went west to Chang'an, raised more than a hundred thousand soldiers, and with Xuan entered Hanzhong through Lu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Shuang reached Chang'an, mobilized over a hundred thousand troops, and with Xuan entered Hanzhong through Lu Valley.

sentences.zh: 漢中守兵不滿三萬，諸將皆恐，欲守城不出以待涪兵。

translations.literal: Hanzhong's defending soldiers did not reach thirty thousand; the generals all feared and wished to hold the city without going out to await Fu's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong held fewer than thirty thousand defenders; the generals feared siege and wanted to wait inside for reinforcements from Fu.

sentences.zh: 王平曰：「漢中去涪垂千里，賊若得關，便為深禍，今宜先遣劉護軍據興勢，平為後拒；

translations.literal: Wang Ping said: "From Hanzhong to Fu the drop is a thousand li; if bandits obtain the pass, it will become deep calamity. Now it is fitting first to send Protector Liu to occupy Xingshi, with Ping as rear refusal;"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping said, "Hanzhong lies a thousand li from Fu; if the enemy takes the pass, disaster follows. Send Protector Liu to hold Xingshi while I cover the rear;"

sentences.zh: 若賊分向黃金，平帥千人下自臨之，比爾間涪軍亦至，此計之上也。

translations.literal: If bandits divide toward Huangjin, Ping will lead a thousand men down to face them personally; by then Fu's army will also arrive—this plan is the uppermost.
translations.idiomatic: if they split toward Huangjin, I will lead a thousand men down to meet them; by then Fu's army should arrive—this is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆疑，惟護軍劉敏與平意同，遂帥所領據興勢，多張旗幟，彌亙百餘里。

translations.literal: " The generals all doubted; only Protector Liu Min agreed with Ping, and they thereupon led their following to occupy Xingshi, setting up many banners and flags stretching more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals doubted, but Protector Liu Min agreed with Ping; they led their troops to Xingshi and planted banners along more than a hundred li of road.

sentences.zh: 閏月，漢主遣大將軍費禕督諸軍救漢中，將行，光祿大夫來敏詣禕別，求共圍棋；

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, the Han ruler dispatched Grand General Fei Yi to supervise the armies to rescue Hanzhong. About to depart, Palace Doctor Lai Min came to bid Yi farewell and asked to play weiqi together;
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, the Shu emperor sent Grand General Fei Yi to rescue Hanzhong; as he prepared to leave, Palace Doctor Lai Min visited to bid farewell and asked for a game of go;

sentences.zh: 於時羽檄交至，人馬擐甲，嚴駕已訖，禕與敏對戲，色無厭倦。

translations.literal: At that time urgent dispatches arrived one after another, men and horses donned armor, and strict carriages were already finished; Yi and Min faced each other in play, their expressions without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent dispatches piled up, men and horses were armored, departure was set—and Yi played on without a trace of weariness.

sentences.zh: 敏曰：「向聊觀試君耳。

translations.literal: Min said: "A moment ago I casually observed and tested you, lord.
translations.idiomatic: Min said, "I was only testing you a moment ago.

sentences.zh: 君信可人，必能辦賊者也。

translations.literal: You are truly a man to be entrusted; you will surely be able to handle the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: You are truly reliable—you will surely defeat the enemy."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day of the month bingchen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day bingchen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 大將軍爽兵距興勢不得進，關中及氐、羌轉輸不能供，牛馬騾驢多死，民夷號泣道路，涪軍及費禕兵繼至。

translations.literal: Grand General Shuang's army was blocked at Xingshi and could not advance; Guanzhong and the Di and Qiang could not supply transport; oxen, horses, mules, and donkeys mostly died; commoners and barbarians wept and wailed on the roads; Fu's army and Fei Yi's troops arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang's army stalled at Xingshi; Guanzhong and the Di and Qiang could not keep supplies moving; draft animals died in droves and people wailed along the roads as Fu's troops and Fei Yi's army arrived in succession.

sentences.zh: 參軍楊偉為爽陳形勢，宜急還，不然，將敗。

translations.literal: Staff Officer Yang Wei laid out the situation for Shuang: they ought urgently to return, otherwise they would be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer Yang Wei urged Shuang to withdraw at once or face defeat.

sentences.zh: 鄧颺、李勝與偉爭於爽前。

translations.literal: Deng Yang and Li Sheng contended with Wei before Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yang and Li Sheng argued against Wei before Shuang.

sentences.zh: 偉曰：「颺、勝將敗國家事，可斬也！

translations.literal: Wei said: "Yang and Sheng will defeat the state's affairs—they may be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Yang and Sheng will ruin the state—they deserve execution!"

sentences.zh: 」爽不悅。

translations.literal: " Shuang was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Shuang took offense.

sentences.zh: 太傅懿與夏侯玄書曰：「《春秋》責大德重。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yi wrote to Xiahou Xuan: "The Spring and Autumn holds great virtue heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yi wrote Xiahou Xuan, "The Spring and Autumn Annals holds great virtue to great weight.

sentences.zh: 昔武皇帝再入漢中，幾至大敗，君所知也。

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Wu twice entered Hanzhong and nearly reached great defeat—as you know.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu twice invaded Hanzhong and nearly met disaster, as you know.

sentences.zh: 今興勢至險，蜀已先據，若進不獲戰，退見邀絕，覆軍必矣，將何以任其責！

translations.literal: Now Xingshi is utmost peril; Shu has already seized it first. If advancing they do not obtain battle, withdrawing they will see interception and cutoff—overturning the army is certain; how will you bear its responsibility!
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi is desperately narrow and Shu already holds it; advance without battle, retreat with the way blocked, and the army is ruined—how will you answer for that!

sentences.zh: 」玄懼，言於爽；

translations.literal: " Xuan feared and spoke to Shuang;
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan was alarmed and spoke to Shuang;

sentences.zh: 五月，引軍還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, they led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 費禕進據三嶺以截爽，爽爭險苦戰，僅乃得過，失亡甚眾，關中為之虛耗。

translations.literal: Fei Yi advanced to occupy San Ridge to intercept Shuang; Shuang disputed the perilous ground and fought bitterly, barely passing through, losses and deaths very many; Guanzhong was thereby emptied and drained.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi seized San Ridge to cut off Shuang's retreat; Shuang fought through the narrows at terrible cost and barely escaped, losing a great host and exhausting Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，秦王詢卒。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Prince of Qin Xun died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, Prince of Qin Cao Xun died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，安陽孝侯崔林卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, Marquis of Anyang, Filial, Cui Lin died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, Marquis of Anyang Cui Lin died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漢大司馬琬以病固讓州職於大將軍禕，漢主乃以禕為益州刺史，以侍中董允守尚書令，為禕之副。

translations.literal: This year, Han's Grand Minister of War Wan because of illness firmly yielded the province office to Grand General Yi; the Han ruler then made Yi Governor of Yizhou and made Attendant-in-Ordinary Dong Yun hold Acting Director of the Secretariat as Yi's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Shu Grand Minister of War Jiang Wan, ill, firmly ceded his provincial duties to Grand General Fei Yi; the Shu emperor made Yi Governor of Yizhou and Attendant-in-Ordinary Dong Yun acting Director of the Secretariat as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 時戰國多事，公務煩猥，禕為尚書令，識悟過人，每省讀文書，舉目暫視，已究其意旨，其速數倍於人，終亦不忘。

translations.literal: At that time warfare was many in affairs, public business troublesome and numerous; Yi as Director of the Secretariat had understanding surpassing others—each time he examined documents, lifting his eyes for a brief glance he had already exhausted their intent; his speed was several times that of others, yet in the end he also did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: War multiplied business; as Director of the Secretariat, Yi's grasp was uncanny—a glance sufficed to master a document, several times faster than others, and he forgot nothing.

sentences.zh: 常以朝晡聽事，其間接納賓客，飲食嬉戲，加之博弈，每盡人之歡，事亦不廢。

translations.literal: He constantly heard cases morning and evening; in between he received guests, ate and drank, played and jested, adding gambling games—each time fulfilling people's pleasure, yet business was also not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He held court morning and evening, yet between sessions received guests, feasted, frolicked, and played games—giving everyone full enjoyment while business never lagged.

sentences.zh: 及董允代禕，欲學禕之所行，旬日之中，事多愆滯。

translations.literal: When Dong Yun replaced Yi and wished to learn what Yi had done, within ten days many affairs were delayed and stuck.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Yun succeeded him and tried to imitate his ways, within ten days affairs piled up in arrears.

sentences.zh: 允乃歎曰：「人才力相遠若此，非吾之所及也！

translations.literal: Yun then sighed and said: "Men's talents and strength are distant like this—it is not what I can reach!"
translations.idiomatic: Yun sighed, "Talents differ so widely—this is beyond me!"

sentences.zh: 」乃聽事終日而猶有不暇焉。

translations.literal: " He then heard cases the whole day yet still had no spare time.
translations.idiomatic: " He worked all day and still could not keep up.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝下正始六年（

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, lower scroll, Zhengshi year six (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part Three (conclusion), Zhengshi year 6 (

sentences.zh: 乙丑，公元二四五年）

translations.literal: yichou cycle, CE two hundred forty-five)
translations.idiomatic: yichou cycle, AD 245)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，以票騎將軍趙儼為司空。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, they made General of Agile Cavalry Zhao Yan Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, General of Agile Cavalry Zhao Yan was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 吳太子和與魯王同宮，禮秩如一，群臣多以為言，吳主乃命分宮別僚；

translations.literal: Wu's heir apparent He and Prince of Lu shared a palace; ritual and rank were as one; many among the officials spoke on it, and the Lord of Wu then ordered separate palaces and distinct staffs;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince He and the Prince of Lu shared a palace with equal honors; after many ministers spoke up, the Wu ruler ordered them separated;

sentences.zh: 二子由是有隙。

translations.literal: The two sons thereby had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: and the two princes bore a grudge from that day.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍全琮遣其子寄事魯王，以書告丞相陸遜，遜報曰：「子弟苟有才，不憂不用，不宜私出以要榮利；

translations.literal: Defender General Quan Cong sent his son Ji to attend on the Prince of Lu and informed Chancellor Lu Xun by letter; Xun replied: "Sons and younger brothers if they have talent need not worry about not being used; they should not go out privately to seek glory and profit;
translations.idiomatic: Defender General Quan Cong sent his son Ji to serve the Prince of Lu and wrote Chancellor Lu Xun; Xun replied, "Talented kin need not fear employment; they must not court favor privately for gain;

sentences.zh: 若其不佳，終為取禍。

translations.literal: If they are not fine, in the end they will invite disaster.
translations.idiomatic: if they lack talent, they will only invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 且聞二宮勢敵，必有彼此，此古人之厚忌也。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear the two palaces' power is matched; there must be mutual sides—this is what ancients deeply dreaded.
translations.idiomatic: And when two courts are evenly matched, rivalry follows—what ancients feared above all."

sentences.zh: 」寄果阿附魯王，輕為交構。

translations.literal: " Ji indeed fawned on the Prince of Lu and lightly made cross-connections and schemes.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji did fawn on the Prince of Lu and lightly wove intrigues.

sentences.zh: 遜書與琮曰：「卿不師日磾而宿留阿寄，終為足下門戶致禍矣。

translations.literal: Xun wrote to Cong: "You do not take Teacher Ri Di as model yet lodge and detain the fawning Ji—in the end you will bring disaster on your household's door."
translations.idiomatic: Xun wrote Cong, "You have not learned from Jin Midi yet harbor this flatterer Ji—you will bring disaster on your house."

sentences.zh: 」琮既不納遜言，更以致隙。

translations.literal: " Cong since he did not adopt Xun's words, further caused a rift.
translations.idiomatic: " Cong ignored Xun and their estrangement deepened.

sentences.zh: 魯王曲意交結當時名士。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu twisted his intent to befriend and connect with the age's famous scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu cultivated the leading men of the day with studied grace.

sentences.zh: 偏將軍朱績以膽力稱，王自至其廨，就之坐，欲與結好。

translations.literal: Partial General Zhu Ji was famed for courage and strength; the Prince himself came to his office, went to sit with him, wishing to bond in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Partial General Zhu Ji was famed for courage; the prince came to his office and sat beside him, seeking friendship.

sentences.zh: 績下地住立，辭而不當。

translations.literal: Ji came down from the ground, stood, declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Ji stepped down and stood, declining the honor.

sentences.zh: 績，然之子也。

translations.literal: Ji was Ran's son.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was the son of Zhu Ran.

sentences.zh: 於是自侍御、賓客，造為二端，仇黨疑貳，滋延大臣，舉國中分。

translations.literal: From this, attendants, bodyguards, and guests fabricated two ends; rival factions doubted and wavered; it spread to great ministers—the whole state was split in two.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter retainers and guests took opposing sides, factions formed, suspicion spread among the great ministers, and the realm divided in two.

sentences.zh: 吳主聞之，假以精學，禁斷賓客往來。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu heard of it, under the excuse of concentrated study, forbade and cut off guests' coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler heard of it, citing the need for diligent study, and barred guests from visiting either prince.

sentences.zh: 督軍使者羊道上疏曰：「聞明詔省奪二宮備衛，抑絕賓客，使四方禮敬不復得通，遠近悚然，大小失望。

translations.literal: Military overseer Yang Dao submitted a memorial: "I hear the enlightened edict reduced and took away the two palaces' guards, suppressed and cut off guests, so that ritual respect from the four directions could no longer pass through; near and far were startled, great and small disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Army inspector Yang Dao memorialized, "I hear that the edict stripped both palaces of guards and barred guests, so that courtesy from every quarter can no longer reach them; near and far are alarmed, high and low dismayed.

sentences.zh: 或謂二宮不遵典式，就如所嫌，猶宜補察，密加斟酌，不使遠近得容異言。

translations.literal: Some say the two palaces do not follow canonical forms; even if as suspected, it is still fitting to supplement investigation, secretly add deliberation, and not let near and far harbor divergent words.
translations.idiomatic: Some say both princes breach protocol; even if that is so, they should be quietly investigated and judged, not left open to rumor from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 臣懼積疑成謗，久將宣流，而西北二隅，去國不遠，將謂二宮有順之愆，不審陛下何以解之！

translations.literal: Your servant fears accumulated doubt becoming slander, long to be spread abroad; yet the northwest two corners are not far from the state—they will say the two palaces have faults of disobedience; I do not know how Your Majesty will explain it!
translations.idiomatic: I fear suspicion will harden into slander and spread; the northwest frontiers lie close, and men will read this as proof of rebellion in both palaces—how will Your Majesty answer them!

sentences.zh: 吳主長女魯班適左護軍全琮，少女小虎適驃騎將軍朱據。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu's eldest daughter Luban was married to Left Protector of the Army Quan Cong; the younger daughter Xiaohu was married to General of Agile Cavalry Zhu Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler's eldest daughter Luban was married to Left Protector of the Army Quan Cong; the younger, Xiaohu, to General of Agile Cavalry Zhu Ju.

sentences.zh: 全公主與太子母王夫人有隙，吳主欲立王夫人為後，公主阻子；

translations.literal: The Princess of Quan had a rift with the heir apparent's mother Lady Wang; the Lord of Wu wished to install Lady Wang as empress, and the princess obstructed it;
translations.idiomatic: Princess Quan feuded with the crown prince's mother Lady Wang; when the Wu ruler wished to make Lady Wang empress, the princess blocked it;

sentences.zh: 恐太子立怨己，心不自安，數譖毀太子。

translations.literal: Fearing that when the heir apparent was established he would resent her, her heart was not at ease, and she repeatedly slandered and defamed the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: fearing the crown prince would resent her once enthroned, she grew uneasy and repeatedly slandered him.

sentences.zh: 吳主寢疾，遣太子禱於長沙桓王廟，太子妃叔父張休居近廟，邀太子過所居。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu lay ill in bed and sent the heir apparent to pray at the Temple of the Prince of Changsha Huan; the heir apparent's consort's uncle Zhang Xiu dwelt near the temple and invited the heir apparent to pass by his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu ruler fell ill, he sent the crown prince to pray at the Temple of Prince Huan of Changsha; the prince's uncle by marriage Zhang Xiu lived nearby and invited him to call.

sentences.zh: 全公主使人覘視，因言「太子不在廟中，專就妃家計議」，又言「王夫人見上寢疾，有喜色」，吳主由是發怒。

translations.literal: The Princess of Quan sent someone to spy and observe, then said: "The heir apparent is not in the temple but goes exclusively to the consort's family to plot," and also said: "Lady Wang, seeing the sovereign bedridden, had a pleased expression." The Lord of Wu thereby grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Quan had him watched and reported, "The crown prince never reached the temple but went straight to his in-laws to plot," and added, "Lady Wang looked pleased at the sovereign's illness." The Wu ruler flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 夫人以憂死，太子寵益衰。

translations.literal: The lady died from grief; the heir apparent's favor daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang died of grief, and the crown prince's favor waned further.

sentences.zh: 魯王之黨楊竺、全寄、吳安、孫奇等共譖毀太子，吳主惑焉。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu's faction Yang Zhu, Quan Ji, Wu An, Sun Qi, and others together slandered and defamed the heir apparent; the Lord of Wu was deluded thereby.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu's partisans Yang Zhu, Quan Ji, Wu An, Sun Qi, and others joined in slandering the crown prince, and the Wu ruler was swayed.

sentences.zh: 陸遜上疏諫曰：「太子正統，宜有盤石之固；

translations.literal: Lu Xun submitted a memorial admonishing: "The heir apparent is the legitimate succession and ought to have boulder-like firmness;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun memorialized in protest, "The crown prince is the legitimate heir and should stand firm as bedrock;

sentences.zh: 魯王籓臣，當使寵佚有差。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu is a feudal subject and ought to have favor and ease with distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Lu is a feudal prince and should receive favor in due measure.

sentences.zh: 彼此得所，上下獲安。

translations.literal: Each obtaining its place, above and below obtain peace.
translations.idiomatic: Each in his proper place, high and low will be secure."

sentences.zh: 」書三四上，辭情危切；

translations.literal: " He submitted the letter three or four times; the words and feeling were perilous and urgent;
translations.idiomatic: " He sent three or four such memorials, each urgent in tone;

sentences.zh: 又欲詣都，口陳嫡庶之義。

translations.literal: he also wished to go to the capital and orally state the meaning of heir and younger sons by birth.
translations.idiomatic: and wished to go to court in person to speak on the rights of heir and younger son.

sentences.zh: 吳主不悅。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler was displeased.

sentences.zh: 太常顧譚，遜之甥也，亦上疏曰：「臣聞有國有家者，必明嫡庶之端，異尊卑之禮，使高下有差，等級逾邈；
