translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Gu Tan, Xun's sister's son, also submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that those who possess a state and family must clarify the distinction between heir and younger sons by birth, differentiate ritual of honor and baseness, make high and low have gradations, ranks and grades far apart;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies Gu Tan, Lu Xun's nephew, also memorialized, "I have heard that whoever holds state and house must mark the line between heir and younger son, set honor and rank apart, keep high and low at distance;

sentences.zh: 如此，則骨肉之恩全，覬覦之望絕。

translations.literal: thus bone-and-flesh affection is preserved whole and covetous hopes are cut off.
translations.idiomatic: then kinship holds firm and covetous hopes die."

sentences.zh: 昔賈誼陳治安之計，論諸侯之勢，以為勢重雖親，必有逆節之累，勢輕雖疏，必有保全之祚。

translations.literal: In the past Jia Yi set forth the plan for securing peace, discussing feudal lords' momentum, holding that though momentum is heavy and kin close, there must be the burden of rebellious conduct; though momentum is light and kin distant, there must be the fortune of preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi once urged policies for order, arguing that great power in a kinsman, however close, breeds rebellion, while light power in a distant kinsman brings safety.

sentences.zh: 故淮南親弟，不終饗國，失之於勢重也；

translations.literal: Therefore the Prince of Huainan, a close younger brother, did not in the end enjoy the state—he lost through momentum being heavy;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liu An of Huainan, the emperor's own brother, never kept his realm—power undid him;

sentences.zh: 吳芮疏臣，傳祚長沙，得之於勢輕也。

translations.literal: Wu Rui, a distant subject, transmitted the throne in Changsha—he obtained it through momentum being light.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Rui, a distant subject, held Changsha for generations—light power preserved him.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝使慎夫人與皇后同席，袁盎退夫人之位，帝有怒色；

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Wen of Han made Lady Shen share a mat with the empress; Yuan Ang withdrew the lady's place, and the emperor had an angry expression;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Han seated Lady Shen beside the empress, Yuan Ang moved her down; the emperor flushed with anger;

sentences.zh: 及盎辨上下之義，陳人彘之戒，帝既悅懌，夫人亦悟。

translations.literal: when Ang distinguished the meaning of above and below and set forth the warning of human-swine, the emperor was then pleased and at ease, and the lady also understood.
translations.idiomatic: but when Ang explained rank and cited the fate of Lady Qi, the emperor was appeased and Lady Shen understood.

sentences.zh: 今臣所陳，非有所偏，誠欲以安太子而便魯王也。

translations.literal: What your servant now sets forth is not partial bias; I truly wish thereby to settle the heir apparent and also benefit the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: What I urge is no partiality—I mean only to secure the crown prince and spare the Prince of Lu."

sentences.zh: 」由是魯王與譚有隙。

translations.literal: " From this the Prince of Lu and Tan had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Lu thereafter bore a grudge against Tan.

sentences.zh: 芍陂之役，譚弟承及張休皆有功；

translations.literal: In the campaign at Quepi, Tan's younger brother Cheng and Zhang Xiu both had merit;
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Quepi, Tan's younger brother Cheng and Zhang Xiu both won merit;

sentences.zh: 全琮子端、緒與之爭功，譖承、休於吳主，吳主徙譚、承、休於交州，又追賜休死。

translations.literal: Quan Cong's sons Duan and Xu disputed merit with them and slandered Cheng and Xiu to the Lord of Wu; the Lord of Wu moved Tan, Cheng, and Xiu to Jiaozhou and further posthumously granted Xiu death.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Cong's sons Duan and Xu disputed merit with them and slandered Cheng and Xiu to the Wu ruler; the Wu ruler moved Tan, Cheng, and Xiu to Jiaozhou and further posthumously granted Xiu death.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅吾粲請使魯王出鎮夏口，出楊竺等不得令在京師，又數以消息語陸遜；

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Grand Tutor Wu Can asked that the Prince of Lu be sent out to garrison Xiakou, that Yang Zhu and others be sent out and not allowed in the capital, and repeatedly sent word to Lu Xun;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Grand Tutor Wu Can asked that the Prince of Lu be sent out to garrison Xiakou, that Yang Zhu and others be sent out and not allowed in the capital, and repeatedly sent word to Lu Xun;

sentences.zh: 魯王與楊竺共譖之，吳主怒，收粲下獄，誅。

translations.literal: the Prince of Lu and Yang Zhu together slandered him; the Lord of Wu was angry, seized Can and put him in prison, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Lu and Yang Zhu together slandered him; the Wu ruler was angry, seized Can and put him in prison, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 數遣中使責問陸遜，遜憤恚而卒。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent palace envoys to rebuke and question Lu Xun; Xun died of rage and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sent palace envoys to rebuke and question Lu Xun; Xun died of rage and resentment.

sentences.zh: 其子抗為建武校尉，代領遜眾，送葬東還，吳主以楊竺所白遜二十事問抗，抗事事條答，吳主意乃稍解。

translations.literal: His son Kang was Colonel of Establishing Martiality, succeeding to command Xun's troops; escorting the funeral east and returning, the Lord of Wu questioned Kang on the twenty matters Yang Zhu had reported against Xun; Kang answered each item by item, and the Lord of Wu's mind was then somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang was Colonel of Establishing Martiality, succeeding to command Xun's troops; escorting the funeral east and returning, the Wu ruler questioned Kang on the twenty matters Yang Zhu had reported against Xun; Kang answered each item by item, and the Wu ruler's mind was then somewhat eased.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，都鄉穆侯趙儼卒。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: the Revered Marquis of the Capital District Zhao Yan died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, the Revered Marquis of the Capital District Zhao Yan died.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，吳將軍馬茂謀殺吳主及大臣以應魏，事洩，並黨與皆族誅。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Wu general Ma Mao plotted to kill the Lord of Wu and great ministers to respond to Wei; the affair leaked, and he and his partisans were all executed to the clan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wu general Ma Mao plotted to kill the Wu ruler and great ministers to respond to Wei; the affair leaked, and he and his partisans were all executed to the clan.

sentences.zh: 八月，以太常高柔為司空。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Minister of Ceremonies Gao Rou was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Minister of Ceremonies Gao Rou was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 漢甘太后殂。

translations.literal: Han's Empress Dowager Gan died.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's Empress Dowager Gan died.

sentences.zh: 吳主遣校尉陳勳將屯田及作士三萬人，鑿句容中道，自小其至雲陽西城，通會市，作邸閣。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu sent Colonel Chen Xun to lead thirty thousand men of agricultural garrisons and construction laborers to cut the middle route at Jurong, from Xiaoji to the western city of Yunyang, connecting market towns and building relay lodges.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler sent Colonel Chen Xun to lead thirty thousand men of agricultural garrisons and construction laborers to cut the middle route at Jurong, from Xiaoji to the western city of Yunyang, connecting market towns and building relay lodges.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，漢大司馬琬卒。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month: Han's Grand Marshal Wan died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, Shu's Grand Marshal Wan died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，漢費禕至漢中，行圍守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Han's Fei Yi reached Hanzhong and conducted encirclement hunts and defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Shu's Fei Yi reached Hanzhong and conducted encirclement hunts and defense.

sentences.zh: 漢尚書令董允卒；

translations.literal: Han's Director of the Masters of Writing Dong Yun died;
translations.idiomatic: Shu's Director of the Masters of Writing Dong Yun died;

sentences.zh: 以尚書呂乂為尚書令。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Lü Yi was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Lü Yi was made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 董允秉心公亮，獻可替否，備盡忠益，漢主甚嚴憚之。

translations.literal: Dong Yun held his heart fair and bright, offered what was acceptable and replaced what was not, exhaustively fulfilling loyalty and benefit—the Han ruler greatly feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yun held his heart fair and bright, offered what was acceptable and replaced what was not, exhaustively fulfilling loyalty and benefit—the Shu emperor greatly feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 宦人黃皓，便僻佞慧，漢主愛之。

translations.literal: Eunuch Huang Hao was facile, fawning, and clever; the Han ruler loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Huang Hao was facile, fawning, and clever; the Shu emperor loved him.

sentences.zh: 允上則正色規主，下則數責於皓。

translations.literal: Yun upward with stern countenance admonished the ruler; downward he repeatedly rebuked Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Yun upward with stern countenance admonished the ruler; downward he repeatedly rebuked Hao.

sentences.zh: 皓畏允，不敢為非，終允之世，皓位不過黃門丞。

translations.literal: Hao feared Yun and dared not do wrong; through Yun's lifetime Hao's post did not exceed Yellow Gate Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Hao feared Yun and dared not do wrong; through Yun's lifetime Hao's post did not exceed Yellow Gate Assistant.

sentences.zh: 費禕以選曹郎汝南陳祗代允為侍中，祗矜厲有威容，多技藝，挾智數，故禕以為賢，越次而用之。

translations.literal: Fei Yi made Selection Bureau Gentleman Chen Zhi of Runan replace Yun as Palace Attendant; Zhi was stern and imposing in bearing, skilled in many arts, and relied on stratagem—hence Yi held him worthy and used him out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi made Selection Bureau Gentleman Chen Zhi of Runan replace Yun as Palace Attendant; Zhi was stern and imposing in bearing, skilled in many arts, and relied on stratagem—hence Yi held him worthy and used him out of order.

sentences.zh: 祗與皓相表裡，皓始預政，累遷至中常侍，操弄威柄，終以覆國。

translations.literal: Zhi and Hao were inside and outside to each other; Hao began to participate in government, was repeatedly promoted to Regular Palace Attendant, manipulated authority, and in the end brought the state to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Hao were inside and outside to each other; Hao began to participate in government, was repeatedly promoted to Regular Palace Attendant, manipulated authority, and in the end brought the state to ruin.

sentences.zh: 自陳祗有寵，而漢主追怨董允日深，謂為自輕，由祗阿意迎合而皓浸潤構間故也。

translations.literal: From the time Chen Zhi had favor, the Han ruler's growing resentment of Dong Yun grew daily deeper, thinking himself slighted—because Zhi flattered intent and complied while Hao seeped in and built divisions.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Chen Zhi had favor, the Shu emperor's growing resentment of Dong Yun deepened daily, thinking himself slighted—because Zhi flattered intent and complied while Hao seeped in and built divisions.
